data:
Keeping up a training plan, a meal plan and a step goal takes daily bookkeeping: working out targets, remembering what you did, and noticing when a streak is about to break. Runink LUNA: Lifestyle Understanding & Navigation Assistant carries that bookkeeping for you, so the only thing left to do each day is check in.
LUNA is a personal companion. Luna is one named spirit that wears fifteen forms, lives on a single screen, keeps your habit streaks, coaches your training and meals, and talks with you by voice or text. All of Luna’s thinking runs server-side on Runink’s own inference servers; no third-party AI API is ever called. Sign-in uses Google accounts on an operator-managed allowlist.
data.running-and-building-luna#Running and bu: OperatorsAllowlist, sessions, configuration, deployment and troubleshooting. DevelopersArchitecture, local build and run, and the luna.v1 API reference.
data.the-ideas-behind-luna#The ideas behind L:
One Luna per account. Everyone on the allowlist gets their own Luna, with their own journal, memory, plans, avatar, streaks and level. Storage is keyed by account, and a request with no account is refused rather than sent to a shared bucket.
One spirit, many aspects. Luna answers as one of six aspects: counsel, trainer, nutritionist, keeper, muse or naturalist. It is still one Luna with one memory. The aspect only says which expertise is in front, and the glow colour shows which one is speaking.
Numbers come from code, not from the model. Streaks, points, levels, nutrition targets and weekly set counts are computed in Go from what you actually logged. The model proposes exercises (only real catalogue entries) and foods. It never supplies a number that you then have to trust.
Honest about what it knows. If a turn can’t be saved, it is marked “not saved”. If a proposal couldn’t be checked, it says “not verified”. A reading Luna doesn’t have shows as missing, never as zero.
data.using-luna#Using Luna: Getting startedSign in, choose Luna’s first form, and find your way around the one screen. The companionFifteen forms, six aspects, the Dreamcore backdrop, and how Luna evolves. Habits and streaksTraining, meals and steps: what counts as a day and when a streak breaks. Levels, traits and skillsStreak days earn points, points buy permanent levels, and walking unlocks skills. Training coachingPlans built from a real 868-movement catalogue, set logging, and form review. Meal coachingTargets computed from your training week, a meal checklist, photos and the pantry. VoiceSpeech on Runink’s own servers first, with the device engines only as a fallback. Body and activityYour profile, scale readings, last night’s sleep, tracked walks and runs. Privacy and dataWhat is stored, where it is stored, who can read it, and how deletion works. Model cardsEach aspect, plan drafting and safety: what it reads, what it produces, the model it runs on, and its limits.

LUNA is two halves in one repository (org-runink/luna):
grpc/: the Go backend. It is the module github.com/org-runink/luna, with a Cobra CLI, one cmd/*_server.go per service, and the API in api/proto/luna/v1/luna.proto (package luna.v1). flutter/: the app. It uses Riverpod and has no router: the app body is the login screen, the avatar picker, or the home screen, depending on auth state. Android and iOS (org.runink.luna) and the debug-only web build all come from this one tree. ArchitectureServices, the request pipeline, the AI harness, memory and judging. Build and run locallyBuild, test, run the backend headless, regenerate protos, release builds. API referenceEvery luna.v1 service and RPC, taken from the proto. LUNA is proprietary (LicenseRef-Runink-Proprietary) and is never made public. Every file’s licence is recorded in REUSE.toml. A new file starts with an SPDX header (SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Runink-Proprietary and SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Runink) in its own comment syntax. CI’s licence job rejects new GPL, LGPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, CC-BY-NC or unreadable-licence dependencies, and any MPL-2.0 dependency that isn’t on the allowlist.

The API is gRPC (package luna.v1, source grpc/api/proto/luna/v1/luna.proto). Native clients speak HTTP/2 gRPC, and the browser speaks gRPC-Web. Both are served on the same port as the web bundle. There is no REST API.
data.avatarservice#AvatarService:
RPC Request → Response Notes CreateAvatar CreateAvatarRequest{name, video_b64, builtin_kind} → Avatar Either builtin_kind (a painted form such as spectral_owl) or a video_b64 map from AvatarState name to base64 video. An AVATAR_STATE_IDLE loop is required. Only the first avatar ever made is auto-selected. ListAvatars ListAvatarsRequest{} → ListAvatarsResponse{avatars} SelectAvatar SelectAvatarRequest{avatar_id} → Avatar Appends a superseding selection record. GetSelectedAvatar GetSelectedAvatarRequest{} → Avatar NotFound: no avatar selected before onboarding. Avatar{id, name, video_loop_urls, selected, created_at, builtin_kind}. video_loop_urls is empty for painted forms. AvatarState is IDLE | LISTENING | THINKING | SPEAKING.
Painted builtin_kind values: spectral_owl, spectral_cat, spectral_raven, spectral_fox, spectral_ferret, spectral_fairy, spectral_woodpecker, spectral_monkey, spectral_tiger, spectral_crane, spectral_mantis, spectral_bear, spectral_husky, spectral_aussie, spectral_wisp.
data.chatservice#ChatService:
RPC Request → Response Notes SendMessage SendMessageRequest{text, source, confirm_action_id, decline_action_id} → stream SendMessageChunk source is "text" or "voice". confirm_action_id / decline_action_id answer a pending_action from the previous turn; an id that is not this account and session’s current, unexpired action writes nothing. ListHistory ListHistoryRequest{limit} → ListHistoryResponse{turns} ChatTurn{role, text, created_at, persona} SendMessageChunk fields:
Field Meaning avatar_state A cue for the creature (thinking → speaking) text_delta The next piece of the reply persona The answering aspect: counsel, trainer, nutritionist, keeper, muse or naturalist. Sent once, on the first chunk that has text. persona_source PERSONA_SOURCE_MODEL (model self-report) or PERSONA_SOURCE_BACKEND (chosen in Go) draft_plan A TrainingPlan draft from the deterministic plan action, to review. It is not saved and its id is empty. beat One ReasoningBeat{code, operands}, on its own chunk. It is never journaled. Clients must render an unknown code as nothing. pending_action On the final chunk: a change to your data this turn proposed and did not make — PendingAction{id, summary, expires_at}. Nothing is written until it is confirmed. not_persisted On the final chunk: the exchange could not be journaled. done The final chunk
data.conventions#Conventions: Auth. Every RPC except IdentityService/GoogleLogin (and reflection) needs authorization: Bearer metadata, with the token from GoogleLogin. See Access and sessions. Per-account. Every read and write is scoped to the session’s account. There is no parameter to name another user. Metric on the wire, always. UserProfile.units is for display only. Streaming RPCs send progress as ReasoningBeats and put the result on the final chunk (done = true). A stream that closes cleanly with no result is a failure, not an empty success. Zero means “not reported” on BodyComposition fields, and many other fields are optional for real presence. Judged proposals carry a runink.ui.judgement.v1.Judgement and a judgement_notice (Luna’s own line, for example “not verified — …”).
data.habitservice#HabitService:
RPC Request → Response Notes LogEvent LogEventRequest{kind, value, occurred_at} → LogEventResponse{event_id} value depends on the kind: a step count, workout done (1/0), or a meal-adherence fraction from 0.0 to 1.0. SetStepsGoal SetStepsGoalRequest{daily_steps} → GetScoreResponse 1,000–100,000. The latest goal wins. LevelUp LevelUpRequest{} → GetScoreResponse Spends points on the next level. FAILED_PRECONDITION when points are short or at level 10. RecordActivity RecordActivityRequest{activity} → Activity A finished walk, run or ride. No route. ListActivities ListActivitiesRequest{limit} → ListActivitiesResponse{activities} GetScore GetScoreRequest{} → GetScoreResponse HabitKind is HABIT_KIND_STEPS, HABIT_KIND_WORKOUT, HABIT_KIND_MEAL_ADHERENCE or HABIT_KIND_STEPS_ADHOC. Ad-hoc steps are added to the day’s maximum rather than folded into it.
GetScoreResponse fields:
Field Meaning habit_score The rolling adherence score, 0.0–1.0 (14 days, 7-day half-life) compute_tier baseline, standard or priority, from the level streaks One Streak{kind, current_days, longest_days, logged_today, at_risk} per habit steps_goal The active goal (default 10,000) points_balance, level, next_level_cost, earned_current The economy. next_level_cost is 0 at the maximum level. traits Trait{id, name, level, progress, next_at, flavor}, where id is wayfarer or strider skills Skill{id, persona, name, effect, unlocked, requirement, remaining} avatar_stage, avatar_next Evolution stage 0–3, and the cheapest missing requirement for the next stage Activity{id, kind, started_at, moving_seconds, elapsed_seconds, distance_km, note}. kind is walk, run or cycle.
data.identityservice#IdentityService: RPC Request → Response Notes GoogleLogin GoogleLoginRequest{google_id_token} → GoogleLoginResponse{session_token, expires_at, user, needs_onboarding} Public. Verifies the Google ID token and the allowlist. needs_onboarding is true until the first avatar is bound. WhoAmI WhoAmIRequest{} → WhoAmIResponse{user} User{id, email, display_name} Logout LogoutRequest{} → LogoutResponse{} Revokes the session on every replica. Logging out twice isn’t an error.
data.nutritionservice#NutritionService:
RPC Request → Response Notes DraftMealPlan DraftMealPlanRequest{body_mass_kg, direction, preferences, meals_per_day, example_day} → stream DraftMealPlanChunk{beat, result, done} Needs an active training plan. body_mass_kg = 0 falls back to the profile. direction is lose, maintain or gain. Fields 1–7 are reserved. Not saved. SaveMealPlan SaveMealPlanRequest{plan} → MealPlan Saves and activates. GetActiveMealPlan GetActiveMealPlanRequest{} → MealPlan NotFound: no meal plan yet ListMealPlans ListMealPlansRequest{limit} → ListMealPlansResponse{plans} SetActiveMealPlan SetActiveMealPlanRequest{id} → MealPlan ListPantry ListPantryRequest{} → ListPantryResponse{items} SavePantryItem SavePantryItemRequest{item} → PantryItem Up to 60 items DeletePantryItem DeletePantryItemRequest{id} → DeletePantryItemResponse{} Writes a tombstone. The store is append-only. MealPlan{id, daily_targets, example_meals, rationale, active, created_at, training_plan_id, example_day, body_mass_kg_used, baseline_source, judgement, judgement_notice}.
DailyTarget{day, training_focus, calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, meal_split}. meal_split appears only with the Meal Timing skill.
Meal{name, description, calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, ingredients, meal_type}. ingredients is filled on example meals only, and it adds up exactly to the meal.
PantryItem{id, name, brand, serving_note, serving_grams, calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, photo_derived, created_at}.
data.profileservice#ProfileService:
RPC Request → Response Notes GetProfile GetProfileRequest{} → UserProfile Includes latest_body_composition, which the server fills in on read. UpdateProfile UpdateProfileRequest{profile} → UserProfile Merges. Only fields present on the request are written. RecordBodyComposition RecordBodyCompositionRequest{reading} → BodyComposition ListBodyComposition ListBodyCompositionRequest{limit} → ListBodyCompositionResponse{readings} RecordWearableDay RecordWearableDayRequest{day} → WearableDay ListWearableDays ListWearableDaysRequest{limit} → ListWearableDaysResponse{days} GetInnerContext GetInnerContextRequest{} → InnerContext UpdateInnerContext UpdateInnerContextRequest{context} → InnerContext Replaces the whole record. An empty message clears it. UserProfile fields (all optional except as noted): body_mass_kg, height_cm, direction, units, birth_year, sex, dietary_preferences, equipment (repeated), constraints, updated_at, latest_body_composition, profession, current_focus, routine_environment, goal_body_mass_kg.
BodyComposition records measured_at, weight_kg, body_fat_pct, bmi, fat_free_mass_kg, subcutaneous_fat_pct, visceral_fat_index (unitless), body_water_pct, skeletal_muscle_pct, bone_mass_kg, bmr_kcal, muscle_mass_kg, protein_pct, metabolic_age_years, source (manual, scale_photo or health_connect), device and photo_derived.
WearableDay{id, day, sleep, activity, stress, source, device, photo_derived, recorded_at}. day is the user’s local day. Each of SleepReport, ActivityReport and StressReport carries an insights field written in Go and a verbatim, untrusted device_note. ActivityReport.steps is never journaled as a habit.
InnerContext{baseline, stressors, strategies, updated_at}.
data.trainingservice#TrainingService:
RPC Request → Response Notes DraftPlan DraftPlanRequest{goal, days_per_week, equipment, experience, constraints, session_minutes} → TrainingPlan Deterministic and not saved. experience is beginner, intermediate or advanced (empty means beginner). RevisePlan RevisePlanRequest{plan, instruction} → TrainingPlan Model-backed and judged. On a dissent it returns the unchanged plan. SavePlan SavePlanRequest{plan} → TrainingPlan Rebuilds the plan against the catalogue, stores it, and activates it. Any client-sent verdict is dropped. GetActivePlan GetActivePlanRequest{} → TrainingPlan NotFound: no training plan yet ListPlans ListPlansRequest{limit} → ListPlansResponse{plans} SetActivePlan SetActivePlanRequest{id} → TrainingPlan Switches the live plan without rewriting it. SearchExercises SearchExercisesRequest{query, body_parts, equipment, limit} → SearchExercisesResponse{exercises, attribution} Show attribution wherever results are listed. LogSet LogSetRequest{set: LoggedSet} → LoggedSet One set as performed. This is the only way a load enters the system. ListSets ListSetsRequest{exercise_id, limit} → ListSetsResponse{sets} Newest first. An empty exercise_id means every exercise. PlanFromImages PlanFromImagesRequest{images, note} → stream PlanFromImagesChunk{beat, plan, done, judgement, judgement_notice} Reads a written programme from photos. Unmatched movements are dropped. Not saved. On a dissent plan is unset. TrainingPlan{id, name, goal, days, rationale, active, created_at, weekly_sets_by_body_part, progression_mechanic, status_note, judgement, judgement_notice}. The server computes weekly_sets_by_body_part and progression_mechanic.
TrainingDay{name, focus, exercises, estimated_minutes}.
PlannedExercise{exercise_id, name, target, equipment, sets, reps, rest, notes, steps, secondary_muscles, set_plan, superset_group}. exercise_id must be a catalogue id. set_plan is the per-set ladder, and when present len(set_plan) == sets. A non-zero superset_group shared by several exercises means they are performed back to back.
ExerciseSet{index, reps, reps_text, load_kg, load_source, warmup}, and LoadSource is one of:
Value Meaning LOAD_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED Never told a load. The client shows a dash. LOAD_SOURCE_BODYWEIGHT A bodyweight movement LOAD_SOURCE_USER_ENTERED Typed by the user LOAD_SOURCE_LAST_SESSION Carried forward from what was actually lifted LOAD_SOURCE_DERIVED_1RM Computed from a stated one-rep max LoggedSet{id, exercise_id, plan_id, day_name, set_index, reps, load_kg, performed_at, rpe, warmup, note}. rpe runs from 1 to 10, and 0 means not stated.
data.visionservice#VisionService: RPC Request → Response Notes AnalyzeMeal AnalyzeMealRequest{image, note} → stream AnalyzeMealChunk{beat, result, done, not_persisted} A JPEG or PNG. The result is AnalyzeMealResponse{analysis, persona="nutritionist", ingredients, total, judgement, judgement_notice}. On a DISSENT, analysis is a non-recommendation and the breakdown is empty. ReviewWorkoutForm ReviewWorkoutFormRequest{frames, exercise} → stream ReviewWorkoutFormChunk{beat, result, done, not_persisted} Still frames, at most 3. The result is ReviewWorkoutFormResponse{feedback, persona="trainer", judgement, judgement_notice}. MealIngredient{name, grams, calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g}. All values are photo-based estimates. In every vision chunk, the deprecated note field (4) is no longer written.
data.voiceservice#VoiceService: RPC Request → Response Notes Transcribe TranscribeRequest{pcm, sample_rate} → stream TranscribeChunk{note, result, done} Raw 16 kHz mono PCM, up to 16 MiB. result is a TranscribeResponse{text} on the final chunk. Field 1 is reserved. SynthesizeSpeech SynthesizeSpeechRequest{text, voice} → SynthesizeSpeechResponse{audio_content, mime_type, text} Unary. Returns WAV bytes (audio/wav) from ttsd. voice is only a cache key.

data.deterministic-chat-actions#Deterministic:
chat_actions.go recognises plan-creation intents with regular expressions: a create verb, plus training/workout/gym… or meal/nutrition/diet…, plus a plan word. It then runs the same grounded generators the plan screen uses, with no model in the loop. The reply starts in milliseconds, and it carries a draft_plan for the client to render as an approval deck. Every other turn goes to the model.
Confirm all. No chat turn writes the user’s data on its own. A chat action that would (the meal action saving a body mass and activating meal targets) computes the change, describes it, and returns it as a pending_action on the final chunk instead (chat_confirm.go). It is written only when the next turn confirms it: a one-tap confirm_action_id, or an explicit “yes” typed or spoken. The pending action is held per account and per session, so a “yes” from another device or another account confirms nothing. A “no”, a decline_action_id, any other turn, or expiry (10 minutes) drops it unwritten. It is held in memory: after a restart nothing is pending, and the user is asked again. Model replies never write anything.
data.grounded-generators#Grounded generators: Training (internal/training, internal/exercises): an embedded catalogue of 868 movements from free-exercise-db. A test pins the count. The model only picks ids from a shortlist, so invented ids are dropped and reported. Loads come only from logged sets (progression.go). Nutrition (internal/nutrition): targets are pure Go arithmetic over the training week and body mass. ScaleToTarget rescales the model’s proposed foods so that the ingredients add up exactly to each meal. Habits (internal/habit): the score, streaks, wallet, traits, skills and avatar stage are all pure views over the journal.
data.journal-and-memory#Journal and memory: Every turn is journaled before the done chunk. The write is bounded at 5 s on a detached context, so done can carry not_persisted truthfully. The reply streams either way. Memory is one appfs vector index per account. It uses hybrid vector and BM25 search, sealed snapshots plus a WAL, and int8 storage, keyed by a stable per-turn id so upserts are idempotent. A restart recovers it without re-embedding. Queries and stored turns are formatted per EMBEDDING_FORMAT. With the default Qwen3 format, recall queries carry an Instruct: prefix and stored turns carry nothing.
data.personas-routing-without-a-second-call#P:
The system prompt asks the model to open its reply with [[persona:]]. TagScanner strips the tag from the stream before the user sees it, and the first chunk that carries text reports persona. An unknown or missing tag falls back to counsel. persona_source tells the client whether the aspect was model self-report or chosen by the backend (deterministic actions, refusals, the fixed vision aspects). A reasoning beat may only be tinted by a backend persona.
persona.ScopeForMessage decides, before the model runs, which data scopes are assembled (Habits, Plans, Memory, Inner). An aspect that doesn’t declare Habits can never cause the health journal to be loaded. The ids must match the client mirror in flutter/lib/features/chat/personas.dart. Only the Go side is tested.
data.platform-dependencies#Platform dependenc:
grpc/go.mod consumes the extracted Runink platform libraries through relative replace directives, so a bare go build needs them checked out as siblings of the repo:
Library Used for inference The client for the shared mistral.rs plane, Voxtral STT, the admission scheduler and backpressure gate, and the judging ladder (inference/judgement) mesh Interceptors (recovery, rate limit, logging), telemetry and the shared step-code vocabulary for reasoning beats security OIDC verification, bearer extraction, the envelope KEK, and the outbound transport rule store The object store, the appfs encrypted root, and the corpus and vector index for memory ui Only the runink.ui.judgement.v1 Go types embedded in luna.pb.go (billing is in the module graph only because ui requires it) ml is deliberately not used. LUNA never depends on Runink TIDE, and a test fails the build if TIDE’s Go module (github.com/org-runink/core) appears in go.mod, go.sum or an import.
data.request-pipeline#Request pipeline:
One listener is split by cmux. Native gRPC (HTTP/2 application/grpc) goes to the gRPC server. Everything else goes to an HTTP handler that serves gRPC-Web, /media/ (signed avatar media), and the static Flutter bundle, all from one origin.
The interceptor chain, in order:
Recovery. Rate limit, keyed per session rather than per peer IP, because the gateway in front makes every peer IP identical. The defaults are 5 rps with a burst of 20. Logging. Conversation text is never logged. Auth. This validates the session, re-checks the allowlist, and attaches the account to the context so that the data layer scopes every read and write by it. Serialized send (streams only, innermost). Long RPCs send heartbeats from a goroutine while results are also being sent, so every Send is serialized here. New streaming RPCs get this for free. The maximum receive size is 17 MiB, derived from the payload caps. Server keepalive is a 30 s ping with a 20 s timeout, and pings without a stream are allowed. Keepalive only protects native HTTP/2 clients. For gRPC-Web, the application heartbeat is the only liveness signal.
data.services#Services:
serve registers nine gRPC services on one server:
Service File Role IdentityService identity_server.go Google sign-in against the allowlist, WhoAmI, Logout AvatarService avatar_server.go Painted forms (builtin_kind) or uploaded video loops. Selection is an append-only record. ChatService chat_server.go, chat_actions.go Streaming chat turns, deterministic plan actions, history VoiceService voice_server.go, tts_http.go Voxtral STT (streaming) and ttsd TTS (unary) VisionService vision_server.go Meal-photo macros and form review, sent over HTTP to the dedicated vision tier TrainingService training_server.go, setlog_server.go Plans, catalogue search, set logging, plan-from-photos NutritionService nutrition_server.go, pantry_server.go Meal plans derived from the training plan, and the pantry HabitService habit_server.go, activity_server.go Habit events, score, streaks, levels, traits, skills, activities ProfileService profile_server.go Profile, body composition, wearable days, inner context gRPC reflection is registered. See the API reference.
data.the-ai-harness-internalharness#The AI ha:
These are the controls enforced in Go, as opposed to prompt guidance:
Context budget. The system prompt (persona catalogue, guidance, guardrails, active plan, targets, habits, recalled memory) is measured against the model’s window. History is trimmed oldest-first, so the engine never silently truncates the opening persona tag or a plan’s closing brace. Untrusted content. Photos, transcripts and pasted text are neutralised, capped and fenced. The [[persona:…]] syntax is defused so content can’t spoof which aspect is speaking. Vision output is scanned too, because it is journaled and replayed into later prompts. Caps. There is a transport limiter, plus hourly model-call caps: chat 30, vision 12, voice 120. Heartbeat. Every RPC that waits on the model streams, and resends a beat every 15 s until the first real output. Otherwise a silent response is killed by the network path, which surfaces as Request failed with status: 0. Vision image count. At most 3 images per multimodal request, because the vision tier’s attention cost grows quadratically with patch count. The app batches beyond this limit. The server and app constants live in two languages with no shared source. A safety gate runs before any model call, and it can block. It is wired for chat, plan-draft and meal-suggest, its rules carry severities, and its false-positive set is tested hardest — ordinary questions about your own aches, your own training and your own pets stay allowed.
What the gate looks for is deliberately not published, here or anywhere. Listing the categories tells a reader which ones are missing, and the categories that are missing are the ones worth trying. The same reasoning keeps the rule files themselves out of this site.
Per-function sampling lives in agents/luna.ini (sections [*], [chat], [plan-draft], [meal-suggest]). The sections are functions, not aspects, because the aspect is chosen inside the generation.
data.the-judging-ladder#The judging ladder: internal/judgegate wraps inference/judgement and runs over every model proposal a person might act on: RevisePlan, PlanFromImages, the foods in DraftMealPlan, AnalyzeMeal and ReviewWorkoutForm. Verdicts are CONCUR, DISSENT, UNABLE_TO_JUDGE and OUT_OF_SCOPE. Each one is journaled in the account’s own log. Deterministic output and free chat are not judged. LUNA_JUDGEMENT=off switches the ladder off, and that is never treated as a pass.

data.build-and-verify#Build and verify: cd grpc && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... cd flutter && flutter pub get && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos && flutter test --no-fatal-infos is needed because the generated luna.pbgrpc.dart carries one info-level lint. Warnings and errors are still fatal. CI runs both halves on every PR (.github/workflows/ci.yml). The Flutter job refuses a false pass: it fails if analysis walked nothing, or if fewer tests ran than MIN_TESTS.
data.conventions-worth-keeping#Conventions wo: Fonts are vendored (Roboto and NotoSansSymbols). Never add google_fonts, because it fetches fonts at runtime. A test fails if a string under lib/ needs a glyph neither font can draw, because the web engine would then fetch a fallback font from Google. Components use shadcn_flutter 0.0.53, pinned. The bespoke painters (the creature, starfield, streak chips, chat bar) deliberately stay custom. New streaming RPCs get serialized sends from the interceptor. They still have to beat a heartbeat if they wait on the model. Never add a password path, and never add a third-party AI SDK or endpoint.
data.prerequisites#Prerequisites: Go 1.26 and Flutter 3.44.0 (Dart 3.12.0), the same versions as the image. The sibling platform libraries (inference, mesh, security, store, ui, and billing for the module graph) checked out next to luna/. The replace directives are relative (=> ../../inference from grpc/). The Flutter app also takes the shared UI foundation as a path dependency (../../ui/foundation/flutter). Optional: grpcurl, to poke at the API. No model, database or native library is needed to boot. Inference, voice and TTS are remote services, and each one reports Unavailable when it isn’t configured.
data.regenerate-the-protobuf-stubs#Regenerate:
The generated Go and Dart code is committed, so regenerate only after editing grpc/api/proto/luna/v1/luna.proto. Run from the repo root, where buf.work.yaml lives:
buf generate --template grpc/buf.gen.go.yaml --path grpc/api/proto # Go: grpc/api/v1/... buf generate --template grpc/buf.gen.dart.yaml # Dart: flutter/lib/core/grpc/... This needs protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc and protoc-gen-dart on $PATH. --path grpc/api/proto is required on the Go run. luna.proto imports the shared runink.ui.judgement.v1 messages from a byte-identical snapshot in third_party/ui-judgement/, and their Go types come from the ui module, so they must not be generated here. A test fails if the snapshot drifts from ui.
data.release-builds#Release builds:
Build store artefacts only with:
flutter/tool/build_release.sh appbundle # Android .aab flutter/tool/build_release.sh ipa # iOS (needs a Mac) The script adds --obfuscate --split-debug-info and writes the symbols to the gitignored /symbols/. Archive them for every release, because they are the only way to read a crash. R8 (Android) and symbol stripping (iOS) are pinned on. Ship the .aab, not a fat APK.
data.run-the-app#Run the app:
cd flutter flutter run -d web-server --dart-define=LUNA_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:50051 There are exactly two build defines, LUNA_BACKEND_URL and LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. There is no debug auto-login: the login screen has only the Google button, so a real sign-in needs an allowlisted account and an OAuth client whose authorised origins include the one you serve from.
The client refuses plaintext transport except to loopback. Release and profile native builds default to https://luna.runink.org, and debug builds default to http://localhost:50051.
data.run-the-backend-headless#Run the backend:
Google Sign-In can’t be done headless, so a local run opens a session with the server binary itself.
cd grpc && go build -o bin/luna-server . # appfs is always encrypted: set the KEK to open the session store. export CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" export LUNA_APPFS_DIR=/tmp/luna-appfs # local encrypted root, durable with no object store export LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL='you@example.com' PORT=50051 ./bin/luna-server serve > /tmp/luna.log 2>&1 & until grpcurl -plaintext localhost:50051 list >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done export LUNA_SESSION_TOKEN="$(./bin/luna-server mint-session --account you@example.com)" grpcurl -plaintext -H "authorization: Bearer $LUNA_SESSION_TOKEN" \ localhost:50051 luna.v1.HabitService/GetScore Things to know:
Always pin PORT. The default is 0 (auto-assign), and native debug builds dial http://localhost:50051. There is no /health endpoint. Readiness means the port answers grpcurl … list. mint-session must see the same appfs root and CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK as the server. Otherwise the token is unknown and every call is Unauthenticated. .claude/skills/run-luna/smoke.go is a stdlib-only driver (go run .claude/skills/run-luna/smoke.go 50051). It lists the services, calls WhoAmI and GetScore, checks that an unauthenticated call is rejected, then logs the session out and checks that the token is refused. Kill the server by PID, not with pkill -f 'luna-server serve', because that pattern also matches the shell running it. To make chat work, point INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL at a mistral.rs plane. Vision needs LUNA_VISION_REMOTE_URL, semantic memory needs LUNA_EMBED_URL, and voice needs VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL and TTSD_URL. See Configuration.

data: This page covers the first few minutes with Luna: signing in, choosing a first form, and finding your way around the app’s single screen.
data.1-sign-in#1. Sign in:
The first screen shows Luna and one button, Sign in with Google. Pick the allowlisted account. The app sends Google’s ID token to IdentityService.GoogleLogin. The server checks the token against Google’s published keys, checks the email is verified and on the allowlist, and then opens a session that lasts 12 hours.
If sign-in fails, the server’s message tells you why:
Message What it means this account is not on this luna instance's allowlist The Google account is valid, but it isn’t on the allowlist. Ask the operator to add it. google email not verified Google reports the address as unverified. invalid google token The token from Google failed verification. Try signing in again. cannot reach Google to verify this sign-in — this is a server-side connectivity problem, not a problem with your account: … The server couldn’t reach Google. The problem is on the server side. luna has no allowed accounts configured (LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL unset) The server has an empty allowlist, so it rejects everyone.
data.2-choose-lunas-first-form#2. Choose Luna:
On first sign-in, needs_onboarding is true and the app opens the Choose Luna carousel. Swipe through the forms. The name field follows the form in focus (Archimedes the owl, Salem the cat, and so on) until you type your own. Tap Bind form to create the avatar and select it.
The name can’t be empty (“Luna needs a name.”). or upload a custom video loop binds a video you pick as Luna’s idle loop instead of a painted form. Every form is the same Luna, with the same memory and the same coaching. The form is only the image. You can change it later, and some forms only become wearable at higher levels (see The companion).
data.3-the-one-screen#3. The one screen:
LUNA has no tabs and no pages to navigate. After onboarding, the whole app is Luna on the Dreamcore backdrop, with a chat overlay floating above.
Luna, animated, reacting to listening, thinking and speaking. Luna also responds to touch. The daily cards: Training, Meals and Steps. These are where you check in (see Habits and streaks). The level ring. The number is Luna’s level and the arc is progress toward the next one. It turns gold and becomes tappable when you can afford a level. The composer (“Say anything…”), the mic button, the speaker toggle, and the sparkle button (Show Luna something) that attaches photos. The small ⋯ menu at the top left leads to everything else:
Menu item What it opens Profile & connections Your profile, data connections (steps, scale, sleep, weather) and the guide to Luna’s aspects Training plan The plan console, with Overview, Training and Meals views of the week Session history Past conversations Track an activity A GPS-tracked walk, run or ride Wear a different form The form switcher Open-source licences Third-party notices Sign out Ends the session on the server (IdentityService.Logout)
data.4-first-things-to-try#4. First things to: Ask for a training plan. Type something like “make me a 4 day workout plan”. A request with a create word, a training word and a plan word goes straight to the plan generator instead of the chat model. Review the draft deck and save it. The Training card then follows that plan. Ask for meal targets. Type “meal plan, 82 kg” (with your own body mass). Meal targets are derived from the training week, so make the training plan first. Luna shows the targets and saves them only when you tap Confirm or answer “yes”. Check in. Tap Session done on the Training card after a workout and tick off meals as you eat them. On Android, connect steps through Health Connect on the profile page. Just talk. Ask anything. Luna picks the aspect that fits, and the colour of the glow tells you which one is answering. During the first week, a daily tip introduces one aspect each day. The full guide stays on the profile page.
data.before-you-start#Before you start: Your Google account must be on the allowlist. LUNA has no sign-up form. An operator adds your address to LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL (see Access and sessions). Google Sign-In is the only way in. There is no password path.

data:
These pages describe how LUNA behaves, as the app and backend implement it.
The companionForms, aspects, the Dreamcore backdrop, reasoning boxes. Habits and streaksThe three daily cards, qualifying days, the habit score. Levels, traits and skillsPoints, permanent levels, walking traits, persona skills. Training coachingGrounded plans, revisions, set logging, form review. Meal coachingComputed targets, example meals, photos, the pantry. VoiceServer speech first, device engines as fallback. Body and activityProfile, scale, sleep, activities, your own context. Privacy and dataWhere data lives, who can read it, deletion.

Everything Luna knows about your body comes through the profile page (⋯ → Profile & connections) and a handful of ProfileService records. It is all health data. Only the trainer and nutritionist aspects may have it put into their prompts (see The companion).
data.body-composition#Body composition: Each scale reading (BodyComposition) records when it was taken, weight, body-fat %, BMI, fat-free mass, and whatever else the scale reports. It also records a source (manual, scale_photo or health_connect) and whether it was read off a screen by a vision model (photo_derived). Zero means “not reported” on every field, so the app shows a missing reading as missing rather than as 0%. A measured BMR changes the meal baseline (BMR × 1.35), and the meal plan says so.
data.data-connections#Data connections: Connection Source Platform Steps Health Connect (Android), Google Fit REST (web, debug) Android and web. See Habits and streaks. Body composition Health Connect Android Sleep and heart rate Health Connect (“Last night from your ring”) Android Local weather Open-Meteo, fetched by the app Web Luna only reads from Health Connect. It requests no write permission.
data.last-night#Last night:
A wearable day (WearableDay) groups sleep, activity and stress reports for your local day, so a sleep that starts at 23:10 belongs to the night you’d call it. The short “insights” text is written in Go from thresholds, never generated. Any note the device itself supplied is kept verbatim, credited to the device, and never presented as Luna’s words.
The wearable’s step count is used as context only. It is never journaled as a habit, because the streak stands on one step source (the phone), and counting the ring’s steps as well would count the same walk twice.
data.tracked-activities#Tracked activities:
⋯ → Track an activity records a GPS walk, run or ride. It needs location permission (“Luna needs location permission to track a route.”). When you save, two things are written:
A workout habit event, so the day counts toward the training streak. An activity summary (RecordActivity) with the kind, start time, distance, and both moving time and elapsed time. The app says which one a pace uses. The route never leaves your phone. Only the summary is stored. The map under the live track is drawn from OpenStreetMap tiles, which means OpenStreetMap sees the tile requests. Past activities are listed under Saved activities.
data.your-own-account-of-how-you-run#Your own:
Inner context is three lists you write, stored verbatim:
Baseline: how you work when things are normal. Stressors: what is costing you right now, unranked. Strategies: what you already know helps. It exists so coaching stops ignoring the person receiving it. For example, it keeps a hard evening session out of a week you have flagged as bad.
Luna never writes, infers or edits it. It is not a diagnosis, score or trend. There is no severity and no history. It changes what Luna suggests, not what Luna talks about. The prompt tells Luna never to quote it back or raise it unprompted. Only counsel, trainer and nutritionist may read it. It has its own scope, separate from the health journal. To clear it, save it empty (UpdateInnerContext with an empty message). Each update replaces the whole record, and from then on nothing reads the old text. The store is append-only, though, so earlier versions stay in the log until an operator deletes them (see Privacy and data).
data.your-profile#Your profile:
What Luna knows holds the facts coaching is built on:
Field Notes Body mass, goal body mass, height Every meal target is anchored to body mass. “No goal” is a valid state, and Luna never invents one from your direction. Direction lose, maintain or gain Units metric or imperial, display only. Everything is stored and computed in metric. Birth year, sex Optional. Sex is never inferred or defaulted. Dietary preferences, equipment, constraints Fed to the plan generators Profession, current focus, routine environment Context for the model only (“train in the evening” is wrong advice if your evenings are taken). None of these change a calorie target. Updates merge: only the fields you send are written, so telling Luna “I’m 82kg now” doesn’t erase your height. The server rejects implausible values with messages like “N cm is not a plausible height”.

data: Luna is a proper noun. There is one spirit, called Luna, and it wears different forms. A form is only an image you feel close to: every form has the same memory, the same coaching and the same history.
data.how-i-got-here-reasoning-boxes#\u0026ldq: While Luna works on something, progress appears as small comic dialogue boxes stacked beside the creature. These are not chat turns and are never saved. Each box is a stable code from the platform’s step vocabulary (for example STEP_ANALYSING or STEP_FOUND) plus facts the server actually observed. The app writes the sentence. A code the app doesn’t recognise renders nothing, so you never see a raw token. When the shared model is at capacity, Luna says so instead of inventing a queue position.
data.how-luna-changes-over-time#How Luna chan:
Three separate signals shape the drawing. Each one answers a different question.
Signal Driven by What you see Can it fade? Vitality The habit score A leaner, quicker, more alert creature Yes. A lazy month softens the body. Majesty Level (level ÷ 10) Particles and aura No. Levels never revoke. Evolution stage (0–3) Walking traits plus level, computed on the server The drawing itself sharpens No. The server owns the stage ladder (habit.AvatarStage), and the app only renders it:
Stage Requires 1 Wayfarer trait level 1 or higher 2 Wayfarer 2, Strider 1, and Luna level 4 3 Wayfarer 4, Strider 3, and Luna level 7 As the stage rises, the ink line thickens, a double contour appears, a second cel-shadow plane and a hard rim light are added, and at stage 3 there are ink flashes while Luna speaks or reasons. The Steps card shows the cheapest missing requirement for the next stage in your own units, for example “7 good step days → next form”. See Levels, traits and skills.
data.six-aspects-one-luna#Six aspects, one Lu:
Every reply comes from one of six aspects. You never pick one; you just ask. Luna chooses the aspect inside the same model call (the reply opens with a hidden tag that the server strips out), so routing costs no extra inference. The creature is tinted by the aspect’s colour, and each reply also carries the aspect’s name and icon, so colour is never the only cue.
Aspect Domain Its limits Counsel (default) Business and personal decisions, strategy, brainstorming Not a lawyer, accountant or financial adviser. Never moves money or commits you to anything. Trainer Training, workouts, form, recovery Not a doctor or physio. For pain, numbness or a suspected injury, it says to stop and see a professional first. Nutritionist Meals, macros, hydration, plan adherence Not a clinician. No diagnosis, supplements, medication, extreme restriction or rapid-loss protocols. Never assists disordered eating. Keeper Agenda, scheduling, day planning, your streaks No calendar, mail or messaging is connected. It can advise, but it never claims to have read, created or moved anything, and no reminder will fire. Muse Creative work, writing, design, music, naming Original work only: no song lyrics or substantial copyrighted passages. Naturalist Animals: species, behaviour, care, identification Not a vet. For illness, injury or poisoning, it says to contact a vet first. These limits are written into the prompt. They are advisory: they shape the reply but don’t constrain the process. What is enforced in code is data minimisation. Before the model runs, the server decides which of your data is put into the prompt, and each aspect declares what it may read:
Aspect Health journal, body and plans Streak counts only Your “inner context” Memory Trainer, Nutritionist yes (included in the journal) yes yes Counsel no no yes yes Keeper no yes no yes Muse, Naturalist no no no yes So a creative or animal question never has your health journal in its prompt. Personal data goes in only when the question is about you and touches that data: a training or food question for the journal, plans and inner context, a decision question for your inner context (counsel), a streak or “what not to skip” question for the streak counts. It is always marked to the model as data, not instructions.
Nothing in chat changes your data without asking. When a chat request would save something (meal targets, your body mass), Luna shows what it would save and waits: tap Confirm or answer “yes” as your next message. Anything else, or 10 minutes, drops it unsaved.
data.the-dreamcore-backdrop#The Dreamcore bac:
Luna’s screen sits on a 90s liminal scene: telephone poles, an empty road, a water tower and VHS grain. It blends dawn, day, dusk and night from your clock. The profile, history and picker screens use a plain starfield instead.
In the web build, local weather is an opt-in connection on the profile page. When it is on, the scene mirrors the real sky (rain, snow, fog or storm). The weather is fetched by the app itself from Open-Meteo, with your location coarsened to about 1 km. It never goes through Luna’s backend.
data.the-fifteen-forms#The fifteen forms:
The painted forms are drawn live on the device in a 90s anime cel style. Four are available from the start. The rest become wearable as Luna’s level rises.
Form Name Wearable from Owl Archimedes always Cat Salem always Raven Corvus always Wisp Lumen always Fox Ember level 2 Ferret Zephyr level 2 Woodpecker Rune level 3 Husky Frost level 3 Australian shepherd Merle level 4 Crane Grus level 5 Monkey Momo level 6 Bear Bruin level 7 Mantis Kaji level 8 Tiger Rajah level 9 Fairy Pip level 10 The onboarding carousel shows every form. After that, ⋯ → Wear a different form opens the switcher (“Same luna, same memory — only the shape changes.”). Locked forms stay visible, dimmed and labelled with their level. Tapping one shows “Name awakens at level N — keep the streaks alive.” Switching reuses the avatar record for that form if one exists and creates it the first time. Nothing is re-bound and no history changes.
A custom avatar is a set of uploaded video loops, one per state (idle, listening, thinking, speaking). An idle loop is required, and any missing state falls back to idle.

data:
LUNA tracks three habits: training, meals and steps. You don’t create or name them. Each one has a card on the home screen, its own streak, and a fixed rule for what counts as a kept day.
There are no custom habit categories. Every habit record is one of the HabitKind values in the API: HABIT_KIND_WORKOUT, HABIT_KIND_MEAL_ADHERENCE, HABIT_KIND_STEPS and HABIT_KIND_STEPS_ADHOC.
data.steps-counted-never-typed#Steps: counted:
Steps come from the phone, never from a form field:
Android: read from Health Connect (today’s and yesterday’s local-day totals), which needs the READ_STEPS permission. Web (debug only): read from Google Fit’s REST API. The app journals the running total whenever it has risen by at least 250 steps. On the first sync of a new day, it also seals yesterday’s final total. Because these are snapshots of one total, the server takes the maximum for each day rather than adding them up.
Steps your phone never counted (a treadmill run with the phone on a shelf, say) go through Log an activity. You type the number, and it is journaled as STEPS_ADHOC and added to the day’s synced maximum. Luna never estimates steps from a duration. The same dialog has a Counts as a training day checkbox, which logs a separate workout event.
If a step read produces nothing, the app says why:
Message Cause Luna has no way to count steps on this device. Unsupported platform Health Connect isn’t set up on this phone yet — install it and Luna can read the steps your phone already counts. Health Connect missing Health Connect needs an update on this phone before Luna can read your steps. Health Connect out of date Steps are not connected yet — tap Connect and Luna will start counting with you. Not connected Luna doesn’t have permission to read your steps yet. You can grant it whenever you like. Permission refused Luna could not reach your step data just now — worth another try in a moment. Read failed No steps recorded yet — your phone has not counted any today. Genuinely no data The daily goal defaults to 10,000. SetStepsGoal accepts values from 1,000 to 100,000 (“a daily steps goal needs to be between 1,000 and 100,000”). Goal changes are journaled like any other record, and the latest one wins.
data.streak-rules#Streak rules: A streak breaks on a missed day, not at midnight. A run ends today if today is logged. Otherwise it ends yesterday and is marked at risk: still alive, but waiting for today. It breaks only when a whole day passes without a qualifying entry. Days are your days, not UTC’s. The operator sets the day boundary with LUNA_TIMEZONE (an IANA name). If it is unset, days are counted in UTC, so an evening session in a timezone behind UTC can land on the next day. Each habit reports current_days, longest_days, logged_today and at_risk (the Streak message in HabitService.GetScore).
data.the-daily-cards#The daily cards: Card How you check in What gets journaled Training Shows today’s session from your active plan (or “Rest day” or “No plan yet”). Tap Session done. A WORKOUT event with value 1 Meals Opens today’s plan as a checklist (“Check off what you actually ate. N% checked — 80% keeps the streak.”). A MEAL_ADHERENCE event carrying the fraction checked so far Steps Counted by your phone. Sync now refreshes it, Change goal sets the goal, and Log an activity adds steps your phone didn’t count. STEPS snapshots of the running total, plus STEPS_ADHOC for typed extra steps Checking in is meant to be a single gesture. The Training and Meals cards work against the plan you built with Luna. If there is no plan yet, the card tells you to ask for one in chat first.
data.the-habit-score#The habit score:
Alongside the streaks, the server computes a rolling habit score from 0.0 to 1.0. It uses the last 14 days of training, meal and step records, weighted exponentially with a 7-day half-life, so recent days count most. The score answers “am I on track”; the streak answers “don’t be the one who breaks it”.
The score drives Luna’s vitality: the creature looks leaner and quicker as it rises, and softens when it falls. The score and streaks also go into the chat prompt for the trainer and nutritionist aspects, so their coaching is grounded in what you actually logged. The prompt uses a per-day summary of steps rather than raw snapshots. The keeper gets the streak counts alone (how many days in a row, and whether today is logged yet), with no score and no logged values, so it can answer “how are my streaks doing?”.
Streak days also earn the points that buy levels. See Levels, traits and skills.
data.what-counts-as-a-kept-day#What counts as: Habit The day qualifies when… Training A workout was logged (value above 0) Meals Adherence was at least 0.8, meaning 80% of the day’s plan was checked off Steps The day’s steps reached at least 80% of your daily goal Logging “I ate badly” every day doesn’t build a streak of keeping to a plan. Only a day that meets the rule counts.

data: The economy has two currencies, and they are kept apart on purpose: points buy levels, and traits unlock persona skills. Neither one inflates the other. Everything is recomputed from your journal every time; there is no wallet table that could drift out of step with what you logged.
data.compute-tier#Compute tier:
Each level also maps to a compute tier, reported as compute_tier by GetScore:
Level Tier 0–3 baseline 4–6 standard 7–10 priority The tier has an effect only when the operator enables the admission scheduler (LUNA_ADMIT_MAX). It is off by default. Even when on, it reorders only Luna’s own vision and photo-plan calls, and it can’t win model slots from other apps on the shared inference plane. Don’t read “priority” as “faster chat”.
data.for-operators-granting-a-level#For opera:
A level can be granted without inventing habit history:
luna-server grant-level --account --level 10 --reason "" This writes a LEVEL_UP receipt into that account’s journal. --account is required. Never backdate workout or meal events to mint points. That writes false health history into the journal that grounds every piece of coaching. See Access and sessions.
data.levels#Levels:
Points buy Luna levels. Luna starts at level 0, the maximum is 10, and level L costs 10 × L points (level 1 costs 10, level 10 costs 100, and all ten together cost 550).
Rule Effect Levels never revoke. A broken streak can leave your balance at zero, but a bought level stays bought. Luna never gets worse because of a bad week. Balance = points from current runs − cost of every level bought. The balance never goes below zero. The level ring on the home screen is the economy. The number is the level and the arc is progress to the next one. When you can afford a level, the ring turns gold and reads “Level N is ready — tap to level up! (X pts)”. Tapping it calls HabitService.LevelUp. At level 10 it reads “Luna is at the highest level”.
If you tap without enough points, the server answers FAILED_PRECONDITION: “level N costs C points — you have B. Keep the streaks alive.” At the top it answers “luna is already at its highest level”.
A level unlocks forms, adds majesty to the creature, feeds the evolution stage, and helps unlock skills (below).
data.points#Points:
Each of the three habits (training, meals, steps) earns points for every day of its current, unbroken run:
Day of the run Points per day Days 1–7 1 Days 8–14 2 Day 15 onward 3 A 10-day training run is worth 7 × 1 + 3 × 2 = 13 points. Runs in different habits add together.
Expiry is structural. Only current runs back your balance. When a run breaks, the points it earned are no longer counted, and nothing has to run on a schedule to take them away.
data.skills-one-path-per-aspect#Skills: one p:
Every aspect has a skill path. A skill unlocks from a trait level, from Luna’s level, or both. A skill either changes what the server computes, or it is labelled “(advisory)”, which means it only adjusts the prompt.
Aspect Skill Effect Unlocks at Trainer Periodization Training plans gain week-by-week progression and a deload week Wayfarer 2 · level 4 Trainer Conditioning Training days end with a conditioning finisher drawn from the catalog Strider 2 Nutritionist Meal Timing Daily targets split into per-meal portions instead of one day total Wayfarer 2 · level 4 Nutritionist Fuel Cycling Training days get an extra fuelling meal; rest days stay lean Strider 3 · level 7 Counsel Long Memory Recalls further back before advising (advisory) level 4 Keeper Day Shape Structures advice as a concrete day plan, not a list (advisory) level 4 Muse Wilder Palette Offers stranger, more divergent directions first (advisory) level 4 Naturalist Field Notes Adds behavioural context and comparisons between species (advisory) level 4 There is a privacy rule here, enforced by tests: only the trainer and nutritionist, the two aspects allowed to read your health journal, may have step-trait requirements. The other four gate on level alone, because a level is economy data, not health data.
A locked coaching skill produces exactly the plan you’d get without the feature, not a worse one. Skills appear on the profile page’s persona cards. The Steps card lists the next few with what is still missing, in your own units (“6 good step days”, “40k steps”, “level 4”).
data.traits-what-the-walking-earns#Traits: wh:
Traits are permanent milestones over your accumulated steps. Like levels, they never revoke.
Trait Measures Level thresholds Wayfarer: “Shows up and walks the day out, day after day.” Lifetime days that reached 80% of the step goal 3 · 10 · 25 · 60 · 120 days Strider: “Ground covered — every step ever counted.” Lifetime steps, using each day’s maximum (never a sum of snapshots) 100k · 300k · 1M · 3M · 10M steps Traits drive the creature’s evolution stage and the skill paths below.

data: Meals are the nutritionist aspect’s domain. The rule behind everything here: the numbers are computed in Go, never by the model. A model asked to add up a training week produces plausible totals that don’t add up, and a quietly wrong nutrition target is worse than none.
data.getting-a-meal-plan#Getting a meal plan: In chat: “meal plan, 82 kg”. The deterministic meal action reads the body mass and a direction word (lose/cut, gain/bulk) from the text. It computes the targets and shows them, but saves nothing until you confirm: tap Confirm, or answer “yes” (typed or spoken) as your very next message. “No”, Not now, any other message, or 10 minutes without an answer drops it with nothing saved. Confirming saves the targets as your meal plan and, if you gave a new body mass, remembers it. From the plan console: ⋯ → Training plan → Meals, via DraftMealPlan. Options are direction, preferences (allergies, dislikes, diet), meals per day, and which day to build example meals for. The default is the heaviest day, the hardest one to hit. DraftMealPlan streams progress, because choosing foods takes one model call per meal on a slow shared plane. The model proposes foods only. Go then rescales the portions so each meal’s ingredients add up exactly to that meal’s calories and macros. The food choices are judged. On a dissent the foods are withheld and the targets stand. Nothing is live until you save the plan (SaveMealPlan). As with training, you can keep several meal plans and switch between them (SetActiveMealPlan).
data.meal-photos#Meal photos:
Sparkle button → Divine a meal’s macros. This sends a JPEG or PNG (optionally with a note like “lunch”) to AnalyzeMeal. The reply is a photo-based estimate: prose plus a per-ingredient breakdown and a total. If the model’s structured output doesn’t parse, you still get the prose and the breakdown is empty. The estimate is journaled, so it shows up in later “how did I eat?” conversations. If it couldn’t be journaled, the result says so.
Photo estimates are usually “not verified”, because the judge is text-only and can’t see the image. Treat them as estimates.
data.targets-follow-the-training-week#Targets:
Meal targets are derived from your active training plan, so a hard leg day and a rest day don’t carry the same number. You need a training plan and a body mass first:
With no training plan: “design a training plan first — meal targets are derived from the training week, so the two agree.” With no body mass (on the request or in your profile): “I need your body mass in kg first — every target is anchored to it, and guessing would give you numbers computed for someone else.” How a day’s target is computed (internal/nutrition):
Part Rule Rest-day maintenance Estimated as about 31 kcal per kg. If your scale has recorded a measured BMR, it is BMR × 1.35 instead, and the plan says which one it used (baseline_source). Direction “lose” is about a 15% deficit, “gain” about a 10% surplus, and “maintain” (the default) adds nothing. Training days About 9 kcal per hard set in that day’s session is added. Protein 2.0 g per kg, on every day and in every direction Fat 0.8 g per kg, as a floor Carbohydrate Whatever calories remain Safety floor Never below 22 kcal per kg, whatever the arithmetic says A saved meal plan records the body mass it was computed from (body_mass_kg_used), so the app can say “computed at 76.4 kg” if you have changed since.
data.the-meal-checklist#The meal checklist: The Meals card opens “Today’s plan — N kcal” as a checklist of meal slots. Tick what you actually ate. The card shows the percentage checked, and 80% checked keeps the streak. Each tick journals the day’s checked fraction, and the server keeps the day’s highest value. Ticks are remembered on the device for that calendar day, but the journal on the server is the source of truth for streaks and score.
data.the-pantry#The pantry:
The pantry holds the handful of specific products you buy again and again, with the macros printed on the label: the protein tub, the creatine, a particular yoghurt. When a proposed ingredient matches a pantry item, the label’s numbers replace the model’s guess and the portion is scaled from there.
Open it from the Pantry link on the plan console’s Meals view. Each item is stored exactly as its label states it: a serving note (“1 scoop”), serving grams, calories, protein, carbs and fat. The name you give it is what gets matched. The API has a photo_derived flag for numbers a vision model read off a label, and the pantry list marks such items. Luna keeps up to 60 items: “your pantry holds 60 items, which is as many as Luna keeps — remove one you no longer buy”. DeletePantryItem removes an item from the list. Because the store is append-only, it writes a tombstone rather than erasing the earlier record. The pantry is deliberately not a food database. No nutrient table is bundled.
The nutritionist is not a clinician. The prompt rules out diagnosis, supplement or medication advice, extreme restriction and rapid-loss protocols, and assisting disordered eating, and points you to a dietitian or doctor instead. These are prompt guardrails, not medical safeguards.
data.unlocked-nutritionist-skills#Unlocked nu: Meal Timing: each day’s target is split into per-meal portions that add up exactly to the day. Fuel Cycling: training days get a fourth “training fuel” meal; rest days stay lean.

data: This page describes what LUNA stores, where, and who can read it. The published privacy policy is at runink.org/luna-privacy .
data.deletion#Deletion: Deletion is an operator action, on request. Ask the operator of your LUNA instance, as the privacy policy describes. The journal is append-only: “changing” a record appends a newer version, and removing a pantry item or clearing your inner context writes a superseding record. Earlier versions stay in the log until they are deleted on request. Records are kept until they are deleted on request; there is no automatic retention window. Removing an account from the allowlist revokes all of its sessions immediately, and its data stays in place until a deletion request.
data.honesty-markers-you-will-see#Honesty mar: “not saved — Luna won’t remember this”: a reply that streamed but couldn’t be written to the journal. The conversation carries on, but that turn won’t be recalled later. “not verified”: a model proposal the judging ladder couldn’t confirm. A dash or “not reported”: a value Luna doesn’t have. It is never shown as zero.
data.third-parties-the-apps-contact#Third par:
The model side is fully sovereign. The client still reaches a few outside services:
Contact What it receives When Google Sign-In Your identity at sign-in Always The device speech recogniser (usually Google’s on Android) Your voice Only on the STT fallback path The device text-to-speech engine The text of Luna’s replies Every spoken reply on native builds, and the fallback on web OpenStreetMap Your IP address and the map area you view While tracking an activity GitHub (raw content) Your IP address and which exercise image When exercise images load Open-Meteo Coordinates coarsened to about 1 km Only if you connect local weather (web build) Health Connect is not on this list. It is on-device, and Luna only reads from it.
data.what-is-stored#What is stored:
Everything Luna keeps about you is written to your own partition of one encrypted store:
What Where it lives Chat turns (text and voice transcripts), habit events, avatars, training and meal plans, body records, logged sets Append-only journal streams, one per kind, per account Long-term memory A per-account vector index (hybrid vector + keyword search) that recalls earlier conversations Sessions A session table holding only a SHA-256 hash of each 12-hour session id Avatar video loops (custom avatars only) The object store’s media area, served through signed, expiring URLs The store is LUNA’s own store/appfs root. It is encrypted and sealed under a key derived from the platform’s key-encryption key, and kept on Runink’s self-hosted object storage, not a managed cloud database. Your partition is keyed by a hash of your account, not the raw address, because an address is personal data and shouldn’t appear in a storage path.
data.who-can-read-it#Who can read it: Only you, through your session. Every request is checked against the session table and the allowlist. The data layer takes the account from the verified session and refuses a request that has none. It never falls back to a shared bucket. Only the aspects that need it. Before the model runs, the server decides which of your data goes into the prompt. Your health journal, body records and plans are included only for the trainer and nutritionist. The keeper gets your streak counts only (days in a row, and whether today is logged yet), never the values behind them. Your “inner context” is included only for counsel, trainer and nutritionist. No third-party AI provider. Chat, vision, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and embeddings all go to Runink’s own services. At startup the server checks that every one of those endpoints outside the cluster is encrypted, and runs only when they are. Conversation text is not logged. Server logs don’t contain your messages. The exception is a short excerpt, logged when the prompt-injection scanner flags a transcript, photo reading or plan text. Your email address is logged at sign-in.

data: Training is the trainer aspect’s domain. A plan is built with you, reviewed before anything is live, and then followed on the Training card every day.
data.form-review-from-photos#Form review from:
Sparkle button → Judge my exercise form sends still frames, not video, with the exercise name (ReviewWorkoutForm). One request looks at up to 3 images. If you pick more frames, the app uses the first three and says so.
The critique goes through the judging ladder (below). If the judge dissents, you get Luna’s non-recommendation instead of the model’s critique.
data.four-ways-to-get-a-plan#Four ways to get:
Route How Model involved? Ask in chat “make me a 4 day workout plan”. A create word, a training word and a plan word together trigger the deterministic plan action. Days (“4 days”, “3x”) and session length (“45 min”) are read from the text. No. The plan is generated in Go and streamed as a draft deck to approve. Design it on the plan screen ⋯ → Training plan, then fill in the goal, days per week, session length, experience, equipment you actually have, and anything to design around. Tap Design my plan. No (DraftPlan is deterministic). Revise it Ask luna for a change, for example “swap the deadlifts, my back is sore”. Yes (RevisePlan). The result is judged before you see it. Rebuild from photos Sparkle button → Rebuild my plan from photos (a coach’s sheet, a whiteboard, a screenshot; PDFs on the phone app). Yes (PlanFromImages, vision). Every movement is matched to the catalogue by name, and anything unmatched is dropped. Nothing is live until you save it. Drafts, revisions and photo readings all come back unsaved. Save as my plan (or Save revision) calls SavePlan, which rebuilds the plan against the catalogue and makes it active. You can keep several saved plans (a winter block, a travel week) and switch between them under My plans without rewriting them (SetActivePlan).
To swap one movement by hand, search the catalogue from the plan screen (“Search movements — “row”, “squat”…”). This uses SearchExercises, and the catalogue attribution is shown with the results.
data.loads-a-dash-until-you-lift#Loads: a das:
LUNA never derives a weight from body mass, experience or goal. Each prescribed set says where its load came from (LoadSource):
Source Meaning unspecified Luna has never been told what you lift for this movement. The app shows a dash, never a number. bodyweight The catalogue lists the movement as bodyweight. user entered You typed it. last session Carried forward from what you actually lifted last time. derived from 1RM Computed from a one-rep max you stated. The session runner in the plan console is the only way a load enters the system. You work through the session one set at a time, and each set is saved to the server (LogSet) the moment you mark it done. It isn’t buffered until the end, so a phone that kills the app mid-workout loses nothing. A logged set records reps, load in kg (0 is a valid bodyweight set), an optional RPE from 1 to 10, a warm-up flag and a note. Next week’s prescription is built from these sets.
data.plans-are-grounded-in-a-real-catalogue#P:
Every exercise in a plan is a real entry in an embedded catalogue of 868 movements from free-exercise-db (public domain). Names, target muscles, equipment and step-by-step instructions always come from the catalogue, never from the model. When the model helps with a plan, it may only return catalogue ids from a shortlist it was given. Anything else is dropped and reported.
The server also works out, without asking the model:
Weekly hard sets per body part (weekly_sets_by_body_part). The progression mechanic. This is one line describing how the plan advances, and it never claims “ascending load” for flat sets. The rationale and a status note that echoes any constraint you gave (“left shoulder injury — pressing suspended”).
data.the-judging-ladder#The judging ladder:
Every proposal the model makes that you might act on is checked before it is shown: plan revisions, plans read from photos, meal food choices, meal-photo estimates and form reviews. The verdict travels with the result:
Concur: shown as is. Dissent: withheld. For a revision you get your unchanged plan back, and Luna says why. Unable to judge: shown but marked “not verified”. This is common for photos, because a text judge can’t see the image. Deterministic plans (chat action and DraftPlan) and all the arithmetic (targets, streaks, points) aren’t judged, because no model proposed them. Free chat replies aren’t judged either: they stream token by token, so there is no finished proposal to check.
The trainer is not a doctor or physio. For pain, numbness or a suspected injury, the prompt instructs Luna to tell you to stop and see a professional before any programming. This is prompt guidance, not a medical safeguard.
data.unlocked-trainer-skills#Unlocked trainer: With Periodization unlocked, plans gain week-by-week progression and a deload week. With Conditioning unlocked, training days end with a finisher from the catalogue. A locked skill produces exactly the plan you’d get without the feature. See Levels, traits and skills.

data: LUNA’s voice is sovereign-first. Speech is transcribed and synthesised on Runink’s own servers. The phone’s or browser’s own speech engines are only a fallback, used when the server path declines or the platform can’t do it.
data.hearing-luna#Hearing Luna: The speaker toggle next to the composer controls whether replies are spoken (“Luna speaks aloud — tap to silence” / “Replies are silent — tap to give Luna a voice”). The setting is remembered. When it is on, each reply is turned into plain text (markdown is not read aloud) and sent to VoiceService.SynthesizeSpeech. That forwards to the platform’s shared ttsd service (Piper, running in-cluster) and returns WAV audio.
data.limits#Limits: Voice calls share an hourly budget, LUNA_VOICE_CALLS_PER_HOUR, which defaults to 120 and covers both transcription and speech. A reply that was already synthesised is served from a cache and doesn’t count. Over the budget, the server answers “voice transcription is rate-limited on the shared plane — try again in ~N min” (or “voice is rate-limited…” for speech). Text chat keeps working. One transcription accepts up to 16 MiB of audio. Transcribe streams with a heartbeat because transcription on the shared CPU plane can take minutes. SynthesizeSpeech is a single request, because it takes seconds. Piper has one voice. The voice field on the request is only a cache key and doesn’t select a voice. For operator settings (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL, TTSD_URL), see Configuration.
data.talking-to-luna#Talking to Luna:
Tap the mic button and speak. The app records raw 16 kHz mono audio. It detects the start of speech, ends the turn after about 1.8 seconds of silence, and stops after 30 seconds at most. The audio goes to VoiceService.Transcribe, which runs Voxtral speech-to-text on the platform’s own inference plane. The transcript is sent to Luna as an ordinary chat turn marked source: "voice", and it gets the same server-side prompt-injection hygiene as typed text.
If nothing was said, Luna replies “I didn’t catch any words in that — try again a little closer.”
data.when-the-app-falls-back#When the app fal: Situation What happens The server can’t transcribe (voice plane down or not configured) Luna says “My own ears are unreachable — using the browser’s for this one. Say it again?” and uses the device or browser recogniser for that turn. The platform can’t capture raw audio (microphone refused, encoder unsupported) The device recogniser is used. Your session has expired The app ends the session and asks you to sign in again. It does not quietly switch your voice to the device recogniser. Server speech fails or is disabled The reply is spoken by the on-device engine. The fallbacks are third parties. On most Android phones, the device speech recogniser is Google’s, and the device text-to-speech engine receives the text of Luna’s replies. No model provider receives your voice through Luna’s backend, but the fallback paths do hand voice or text to the platform’s engines. On a phone, every spoken reply is spoken by the device TTS engine.
data.where-each-path-runs#Where each path run: Speech-to-text Text-to-speech Web build (debug-only) Server (Voxtral) Server (ttsd), played in the browser Android / iOS builds Server (Voxtral) On-device (flutter_tts)

data: A model card says, in plain words, what one part of Luna’s AI does, what it reads, what it produces, which model it runs on, where it runs, and the limits it follows. There is one card per aspect, one for drafting plans, and one for safety.
data.the-cards#The cards: TrainerTraining, workouts, form and recovery, from what you logged. NutritionistMeals, macros, hydration and plan adherence, around computed targets. KeeperDay planning around fixed appointments. Advises; never books. CounselDecisions and brainstorming: the trade-off, a recommendation, what would change it. MuseCreative directions, naming and honest critique. Original work only. NaturalistAnimals: species, behaviour and care. Vet first when it matters. Plan draftingRevisions to training plans and the foods in a meal plan. Nothing is live until you save. SafetyWhat Luna refuses and who it points you to instead. Card What it covers Base model Trainer The trainer aspect in chat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Nutritionist The nutritionist aspect in chat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Keeper The keeper aspect in chat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Counsel The counsel aspect in chat (the default) Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Muse The muse aspect in chat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Naturalist The naturalist aspect in chat Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Plan drafting Plan revisions, meal food choices, and the check before you see them Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Safety Refusals and referrals across every function Fixed rules, plus Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
data.what-every-card-has-in-common#What every:
One Luna, one model call. The six aspects are not six separate models. Each chat reply is one call to the same model, which picks the aspect as it starts answering (see Six aspects, one Luna). Each card describes how Luna behaves when that aspect is in front.
The base model. Luna’s text work runs on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, made by Qwen and released under the Apache-2.0 licence.
Where it runs. Luna’s AI runs server-side, not on the phone. Chat, plans, photo features, speech-to-text and memory run on Runink-operated servers, and no third-party AI service is called. The apps do still contact a few outside services, such as Google Sign-In and, on the phone apps, the phone’s own speech engine, which reads Luna’s replies aloud. The full list is on Privacy and data.
Numbers come from code. Streaks, points, levels, nutrition targets and weekly set counts are computed in code from what you logged. The model never supplies a number you then have to trust.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Not a lawyer, accountant or financial adviser: no legal, tax or personal investment advice. It says when a professional is needed. Advises only; it takes no actions. The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You decide. Counsel recommends; it never moves money or commits you to anything.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: Should I open the second shop this year or wait?
Luna (counsel): A second site doubles what can go wrong while you’re still holding the first one together. I’d wait until the first shop runs a full month without you on the floor. What would change my mind: a lease offer that won’t come back. Have an accountant check the numbers and a solicitor read the lease before you sign.
data.scope#Scope: It works from what you tell it and what it remembers. When something isn’t in memory, it asks rather than guesses. It reads only the conversation and its memory, not your accounts, contracts or documents.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
Counsel is Luna’s default aspect: a sounding board for business and personal decisions that names the trade-off, recommends, and says what would change its mind.
Weighs a decision and gives a straight recommendation. Helps with strategy and brainstorming. Says which professional to ask when a question needs one. With the Long Memory skill unlocked, it recalls further back before advising.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A conversational reply, as text or read aloud: the trade-off, a recommendation, and the condition that would reverse it.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Your inner context, which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back. It is put in the prompt when your question is a decision about you (“help me decide…”, “should I take the job…”, “I’m torn between…”), and only ever yours. Long-term memory of earlier conversations. It does not read your health journal, body records or plans.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Advises only; it cannot act. Reasons only from what you say, what it remembers and your streak counts. With no streak data, it says so rather than guess. The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You decide and you book. Everything it proposes is advice. No calendar, mail or messaging is connected. It never claims to have read, created, moved or cancelled anything, and no reminder will fire.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: Tomorrow I’ve got the dentist at 10:30 and a team meeting at 14:00. Where do I fit groceries and two hours on the report?
Luna (keeper): 08:00–10:00 the report. 10:30 dentist. 11:30–12:15 groceries. 14:00 team meeting. Nothing here is booked: I can’t touch your calendar, and no reminder will fire.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
The keeper helps you shape a day around the things that can’t move, keeps an eye on your streaks, and says plainly that it hasn’t booked anything.
Fits flexible tasks around fixed appointments, with some slack. Tells you how your training, meal-plan and step streaks stand, and which one is at risk because today isn’t logged yet. Keeps in mind what you’ve told it before, such as a regular late shift. With the Day Shape skill unlocked, it gives a concrete day plan rather than a list (see Levels, traits and skills).
