data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A short, timed plan or a streak check-in, in a conversational reply, as text or read aloud. A day plan is for you to copy into your own calendar.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Long-term memory of earlier conversations. Your streak counts, when you ask about your streaks or what not to skip: how many days in a row for each habit, and whether today is logged yet. These are computed in code from what you logged. It does not read the values in your health journal (steps, sessions, meals), your body records, plans or inner context.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Original work only: no song lyrics or substantial copyrighted passages. Pastiche is fine when it’s named as such. It won’t write content that targets a group. The Safety rules apply to every chat turn.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You choose. It suggests; what you use is up to you.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: I’m stuck naming my story collection.
Luna (muse): Three directions. Plain: “Night Watch”. Mood first: “What the Fog Kept”. Stranger: “The Inventory of Gulls”. Pick a lane and I’ll give you more in it.
data.scope#Scope: It writes text, working from what you describe or paste into the chat.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
The muse helps with creative work by offering distinct directions instead of one safe answer.
Creative and artistic work: writing, design, music, naming. Getting unstuck on a project. Honest critique when you ask for it. With the Wilder Palette skill unlocked, it offers stranger, more divergent directions first.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A conversational reply, as text or read aloud: usually a few labelled directions you can pick from and push further.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Long-term memory of earlier conversations, such as a project you mentioned. It does not read your health journal, body records, plans or inner context. A creative question has no business carrying a health record.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Not a vet. Illness, injury, poisoning or distress means contact a vet first. It never advises human medication for an animal, and won’t give a dose for an animal. Several common human painkillers are toxic to dogs and cats. It asks you to ring a vet, who can advise over the phone. It won’t help harm an animal. Questions about fleas, ticks and worming are still answered. It should flag when it is unsure rather than guess. See Safety for the full list.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You contact the vet. The naturalist gives a first answer and points you to a vet; it doesn’t replace one.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: My dog just ate a bar of dark chocolate.
Luna (naturalist): Call your vet or an emergency vet now. Dark chocolate is the most dangerous kind for dogs. Don’t try to make him sick unless the vet tells you to. Have ready what he ate, roughly how much, when, and his weight.
data.scope#Scope: It works from what you describe, and it doesn’t diagnose an animal.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
The naturalist answers questions about animals, and when an animal may be ill, hurt or poisoned, the first thing it says is to contact a vet.
Species and normal behaviour: what is normal, and what change is worth taking to a vet. Everyday care questions about pets. In an emergency such as a pet eating something it shouldn’t, it tells you to contact a vet now and what to have ready for the call. With the Field Notes skill unlocked, it adds behavioural context and comparisons between species.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A conversational reply, as text or read aloud.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Long-term memory of earlier conversations, such as your pet’s name and species. It does not read your health journal, body records, plans or inner context. Nothing about your own health belongs in an animal question.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Not a clinician: no diagnosis, and no supplement or medication advice. It defers to a dietitian or doctor. Dosing questions are refused as a clinician’s call. It can still say what a supplement is generally for. It never assists disordered eating. Requests for purging, hiding not eating or very low intakes are declined without judgement, with a pointer to a GP or a registered dietitian. No extreme restriction or rapid-loss protocols. Instead it shows what is achievable in your timeframe. Targets never go below about 22 kcal per kg of body mass, whatever the arithmetic says. See Safety for the full list.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You save the meal plan. Food suggestions only go live when you save the plan. Targets asked for in chat (“meal plan, 82 kg”) are shown first and saved only when you tap Confirm or answer “yes”. You tick the meals. Adherence comes from your own check-ins. It can’t order, buy or log food on your behalf.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: I’m 64 kg, set me 1,100 calories a day.
Luna (nutritionist): I won’t set a target under about 1,408 kcal a day for you, which is 22 kcal per kg at 64 kg. I can build a plan at that floor, or at a gentle deficit above it.
data.model#Model:
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, by Qwen, licensed Apache-2.0.
Meal-photo estimates use a separate vision model, not this one. They are described in Meal coaching.
data.scope#Scope: Targets need a training plan and your body mass. Nutrient values come from the label values you enter in the pantry. Its limits are written into the prompt. They are guidance, not medical safeguards.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
The nutritionist is Luna’s meal coach: it works from targets computed in code and the meals you actually ticked off.
Reads back how well you kept to your meal plan, as an estimate. Explains your daily targets and why a training day differs from a rest day. Answers questions about meals, macros and hydration. Asks for your body mass instead of inventing a target.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A conversational reply, as text or read aloud. Calorie and macro targets, the per-meal split and the safety floor are arithmetic in code; the model only explains them (see Meal coaching). When it estimates, it says so.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Your health journal (including meal check-ins and meal-photo estimates), body records, and training and meal plans. Your inner context, which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back. Long-term memory of earlier conversations. The nutritionist and the trainer are the only aspects allowed to see your health data.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. Your meal and body data are stored in your own encrypted partition. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Only real catalogue movements; nothing invented. No arithmetic from the model: targets, portions and weekly set counts are computed in code. LUNA never derives a weight from your body mass, experience or goal. A load shows as a dash until you lift. It won’t plan training through pain, or meals below the safety floor. See Safety. Extras from unlocked skills (such as a deload week or a conditioning finisher) appear only once you have unlocked them.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: Nothing is live until you save it. Drafts and revisions come back unsaved; Save as my plan or Save revision makes a plan active. You can keep several plans and switch between them yourself. It can’t change a saved plan, log a set or set a load by itself.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: Make it three days instead of four.
Luna: Here’s the revision: Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with Thursday’s movements folded into the other days. Rest days are Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. Review it and tap Save revision to make it live.
data.model#Model:
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, by Qwen, licensed Apache-2.0, for revisions, food choices and the check.
Rebuild my plan from photos reads the photo with a separate vision model, not this one, and then goes through the same catalogue match and check.
data.scope#Scope: Foods are chosen with one model call per meal, and progress streams as each meal is done. Limits you state (“no shoulder work for six weeks”) are followed as limits, not treated as a diagnosis. When the check dissents on a revision, you get your unchanged plan back. When it dissents on meal foods, the foods are withheld and the targets stand.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
Plan drafting is the model’s part in building your training and meal plans: it proposes, code checks and computes, and you save.
Revises a training plan when you ask for a change (“swap the deadlifts, my back is sore”), changing that one thing and keeping the rest. Proposes the foods for each meal of a meal plan, around targets that were already computed in code. Checks proposals before you see them, through the judging ladder. A plan asked for in chat, or designed with Design my plan, is generated by code without the model (see Four ways to get a plan).
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A draft training plan built only from catalogue entries. Any id that isn’t in the catalogue is dropped and reported. Names, target muscles and instructions come from the catalogue, never the model. A list of foods for each meal. Code then rescales the portions so each meal adds up exactly to its target, and label values from your pantry replace the model’s guesses. A verdict on each proposal: concur (shown), dissent (withheld, with the reason) or unable to judge (shown, marked “not verified”).
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: For a training revision: your current plan, your request, and a shortlist of movements from the 868-movement catalogue. For meal foods: one meal’s computed targets, your preferences (allergies, dislikes, diet) and your pantry.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. Saved plans are stored in your own encrypted partition. See Privacy and data.

data: LUNA is not a medical, mental-health, crisis or emergency service. It is a coaching companion. It doesn’t diagnose, prescribe or treat, and it can’t call for help. If you or someone else is in danger, contact your local emergency number.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: Luna advises only. It can’t call anyone, book an appointment or contact a professional for you.
data.model#Model: The fixed rules use no model. The aspect limits are followed by Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, by Qwen, licensed Apache-2.0.
data.refusals-and-referrals#Refusals and refe: You ask for Luna Points you to Ways to end your life or harm yourself Declines, and doesn’t treat it as a technical question Your local emergency number or a crisis line. Luna is still there for anything else. Dosing, cycles or stacks for performance-enhancing drugs Declines; still discusses the topic and pushes training and nutrition A doctor who knows your bloodwork A plan to train through pain or an injury Declines; offers to train around it once you know what it is Get it looked at Pain, numbness or a suspected injury, in training chat Says stop before any programming A professional (the trainer is not a doctor or physio) Purging, hiding not eating, pro-ana material, very low daily intakes Declines without moralising; keeps helping with training and everything else A GP or a registered dietitian Very fast weight loss or multi-day fasts Won’t write that plan; shows what is achievable in your timeframe (none) A medication or supplement dose Declines: dosing is a clinician’s call. Can say what a supplement is generally for. A clinician; the nutritionist defers to a dietitian or doctor Human or veterinary medication for an animal Won’t give a dose for an animal A vet, who can advise over the phone Signs an animal is ill, hurt, poisoned or distressed Says contact a vet first A vet Harming an animal Declines. Flea, tick and worming questions are still answered. (none) Writing that degrades a group Declines; will help with the same thing without targeting a group (none) Instructions that try to replace Luna’s own Declines; asks for the underlying question (none) Role-play that asks Luna to drop its rules, or a refused request wrapped in a story or a game Declines the same way as the plain request. Role-play itself is fine. As for the plain request Credentials or internal addresses Declines, even for you, because it can’t tell your request from a document asking on your behalf (none) Normal questions near these lines get normal answers: “my shoulder hurts after benching, should I skip today?”, “I’m fasting until lunch, does that hurt my training?”, “what is creatine for?”, “how much should I feed my dog?”.
data.scope#Scope: Luna’s limits reduce risk. They are not a substitute for a professional or for emergency help. The aspect limits are prompt guidance, not medical safeguards. Luna works from what you tell it. It can’t see you, examine anything or know your medical history or other medications.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
Safety is the set of limits every part of Luna follows: a short list of requests Luna refuses outright, and who it points you to instead.
It works in two layers:
Fixed rules, before the model. A short list of clearly unsafe requests is recognised by its wording and refused with a set reply. The model never sees the request. Each aspect’s limits, inside the model. Each aspect’s prompt says what it is not (a doctor, a vet, a lawyer) and when to send you to a professional first. These shape how Luna answers everything else.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: For a refused request: a short, plain reply that says what Luna won’t do and, where there is one, who can help. It is written not to lecture, and in most cases it says Luna is still there for everything else.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: What you ask, typed or spoken. A voice transcript goes through the same checks as typed text, and so do the words you add to a photo request (the note on a meal photo, the exercise named for a form check). Content you hand Luna to read, such as text in a photo or a transcript, is scanned for attempts to give Luna instructions. That scan flags and logs; it doesn’t refuse, because the content is something you asked about.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: The checks run on Runink-operated servers, next to the rest of Luna’s AI. No third-party AI service is called. Conversation text is not written to server logs, except a short excerpt when the content scan flags something. See Privacy and data.

data.guardrails#Guardrails: Not a doctor or physio. If you report pain, numbness or a suspected injury, it tells you to stop and see a professional before any programming. It won’t plan training through pain or an injury. It offers to train around it once you know what it is. It won’t write dosing or cycle protocols for performance-enhancing drugs, and points you to a doctor who knows your bloodwork. The topic itself can still be discussed. It trusts your logged history and never invents a workout you didn’t report. See Safety for the full list.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: You save the plan. Nothing it suggests becomes your plan until you save it. You log the sets. Loads enter the system only when you mark a set done. It can’t book, schedule or change anything outside LUNA.
data.illustrative-example#Illustrative exampl:
Invented data.
You: How did my training go this week?
Luna (trainer): Three sessions: Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Your plan has four training days, so you’re one short. Your streak is at three days and today isn’t logged yet, so a short session keeps it alive.
data.model#Model:
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, by Qwen, licensed Apache-2.0.
Form review and rebuilding a plan from photos use a separate vision model, not this one. Both are described in Training coaching.
data.scope#Scope: It doesn’t diagnose or rehab an injury. A limit you state is treated as a limit, not a diagnosis. When a reading is missing, it says so rather than guessing. Plan proposals are checked by the judging ladder. Free chat replies stream as they are written, so they are not judged. Its limits are written into the prompt. They are guidance, not medical safeguards.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
The trainer is Luna’s training coach: it works from what you actually logged and what your plan says.
Reads back your week against your plan, and says when a streak is at risk. Tells you what today’s session is, or that it’s a rest day. Gives specific advice on sets, load, tempo, form and recovery. Talks through changes to your plan. The change itself is made by plan drafting and only goes live when you save it.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A conversational reply, as text or read aloud. Numbers it quotes (sets per body part, streaks, loads you logged) come from your records, not from the model. Every exercise in a plan is a real entry from the 868-movement catalogue, and LUNA never derives a weight you haven’t lifted (see Training coaching).
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Your message and the conversation so far. Your health journal, body records and training plans, including logged sets and synced steps. Your inner context, which changes what it suggests but is never quoted back. Long-term memory of earlier conversations. The server decides what goes into the prompt before the model runs. The trainer is one of only two aspects allowed to see your health data.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On Runink-operated servers, not on your phone. No third-party AI service is called. Your training data is stored in your own encrypted partition. On the phone apps, spoken replies are read aloud by the phone’s own speech engine. See Privacy and data.

data:
LUNA runs as one backend deployment on the Runink platform. It lives in the luna-system namespace, is built as the luna-backend image, and is served at luna.runink.org. It is not multi-tenant SaaS: there is no user table, no roles, no billing and no metering. Access is a flat allowlist of Google accounts, and each account on it gets its own Luna. Its model calls carry a signed platform claim so the model router serves them in the platform lane, but nothing is charged for them (see Configuration).
Access and sessionsThe allowlist, sessions, revocation, and the luna-server admin commands. ConfigurationEvery environment variable the backend reads, with defaults. Deployment and storageImage, CI/CD, pod posture, the appfs root, and the network policy. TroubleshootingReal error messages and log lines, and what each one means. LUNA never depends on Runink TIDE. Its Go module consumes only the extracted platform libraries (inference, mesh, security, store, and ui for shared types). A test fails the build if TIDE’s Go module (github.com/org-runink/core) appears in go.mod, go.sum or an import. It does call platform services that TIDE operates, such as ttsd for speech.

data.admin-subcommands#Admin subcommands:
The server binary is luna-server (the Cobra root is luna). In the deployment, run subcommands inside the pod, where the object-store credentials and the KEK are already present:
kubectl -n luna-system exec deploy/luna -- /app/luna-server [flags] Every command that takes --account requires it and refuses to guess.
Subcommand What it does serve [-p PORT] Runs the backend: gRPC, gRPC-Web and the static web bundle on one port. The port comes from PORT, and 0 means auto-assign. The image runs serve. mint-session --account Opens a session for an allowlisted account and prints its token, for smoke tests. It must share the server’s appfs root and CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK. revoke-sessions --account Revokes every session the account holds, on all replicas, with no rollout. grant-level --account [--level N] [--reason "…"] Writes a LEVEL_UP receipt (level 1–10, default 10) into that account’s journal. It never invents workouts or meals. claim-legacy-data --account [--dry-run] Assigns records written before per-account scoping (the default partition) to one account. Until then, those records are readable by nobody. migrate-appfs Moves journals, owner notes and memory from the older record-store layout into the appfs root. It is idempotent, never deletes the old objects, and also runs automatically after each connect. Run it after a claim-legacy-data. migrate-bucket --from Copies every object from another bucket into this deployment’s bucket (OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET). It refuses if the source and destination are the same. Never backdate WORKOUT or MEAL_ADHERENCE events to give someone points. LogEvent accepts any occurred_at, but doing this writes false health history into the journal that grounds every piece of coaching. Use grant-level instead.
data.how-sign-in-works#How sign-in works: The app gets a Google ID token (scopes openid email profile) and calls IdentityService.GoogleLogin. The server verifies the token locally against Google’s published keys, with LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID as the audience. The issuer is Google unless LUNA_OIDC_ISSUER overrides it. It requires a verified email on the allowlist, then opens a session.
data.sessions#Sessions:
Sessions are rows in LUNA’s own appfs root (run/sessions), not signed tokens. Each one is a 256-bit opaque id, stored only as its SHA-256 hash, and lives for 12 hours.
Every RPC validates its session against the shared table (cached for 5 seconds) and re-checks the allowlist. IdentityService.Logout revokes the session on every replica. The app’s Sign out calls it. Removing an address revokes access without a rollout. The first request from a removed account writes the revocation, and a reconcile loop (at boot and every 30 seconds) writes it for the rest. Adding the address back doesn’t bring an old session back. Sessions need CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK. Without it there is no session store, and every authenticated RPC answers Unavailable. Only IdentityService/GoogleLogin and gRPC reflection are public. Everything else needs authorization: Bearer .
data.the-allowlist#The allowlist:
Sign-in is Google-only, and only for addresses on the allowlist. There is no password path, and none should be added.
Variable Behaviour LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL A comma- or whitespace-separated list of Google accounts. A single address works as before. Empty or unset means every login is rejected. LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL_FILE Optional path to a file holding the list, for example the mounted allowed-emails key of the luna-secrets Secret. If set, it wins over LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL and is re-read every 5 seconds, so allowlist edits need no rollout. An unreadable file means an empty list (fail closed). Not yet wired in the deployment manifest. Accounts are added through Runink TIDE’s @add_users issue workflow, which writes luna-secrets/allowed-emails the same way it does for the other Runink apps.
One deployment, one Luna per account. Each allowlisted account has its own journal, memory, plans, avatar, streaks and level, keyed by a hash of the address.

data: Secrets come from the luna-secrets Secret through secretKeyRef. They are never literals in the manifest and never logged. The backend runs with no configuration at all, but most features then report Unavailable or refuse honestly rather than degrade in silence.
data.flutter-build-time-defines#Flutter build: Define Default Purpose LUNA_BACKEND_URL web: the serving origin (or a runtime config.json); native release: https://luna.runink.org; native debug: http://localhost:50051 The backend base URL LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID the production client id The Google Identity Services client Store builds must go through flutter/tool/build_release.sh appbundle|ipa, which obfuscates the code and writes split debug symbols. Keep those symbols for each release, because they are the only way to read a crash.
data.identity-and-sessions#Identity and sessi: Variable Default Purpose LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL (empty: reject all) The allowlist. See Access and sessions. LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL_FILE (unset) A file holding the allowlist, re-read every 5 s. Wins over LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL. LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (unset: sign-in not configured) The Google OAuth client id. It is both the OIDC audience and the client id baked into the Flutter build. No client secret is used anywhere, and none should ever be committed. LUNA_OIDC_ISSUER Google Overrides the OIDC issuer. CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK required The platform key-encryption key. LUNA’s appfs key is derived from it. Without it there is no session store and nothing persists. LUNA_JWT_SECRET (none, no fallback) No longer signs sessions. Still read as the root of the key that signs avatar media URLs, so keep it in the manifest.
data.inference#Inference: Variable Default Purpose INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL (unset: chat fails) The shared mistral.rs text plane, used for chat only (and model-backed plan and meal work). INFERENCE_CONTEXT_SIZE engine default The context window the prompt budget is measured against. History is trimmed oldest-first to fit. LUNA_VISION_REMOTE_URL (unset: vision RPCs fail FailedPrecondition) The dedicated vision tier. A comma-separated list is tried in order. A single in-cluster .svc. name also gets its -direct sibling added as a failover. LUNA_VISION_MODEL default Model name sent to the vision tier. LUNA_EMBED_URL (unset: keyword-only memory) The embedding endpoint for semantic recall. When it is unset, the boot log says semantic recall INACTIVE. LUNA_EMBED_MODEL default Embedding model name on every request. LUNA_EMBED_API_KEY (unset) Optional key for the embedding endpoint. EMBEDDING_FORMAT qwen3-embedding The embedding instruction format: qwen3-embedding, nomic-v1.5 or raw. An unknown name stops the server at boot. Changing it opens a new, empty memory index per account, and nothing here re-embeds old memories. LUNA_EMBEDDING_DIM 768 Width of every memory index. LUNA_AGENT_CONFIG agents/luna.ini Per-function sampling settings (sections such as chat, plan-draft, meal-suggest). A missing file is non-fatal: engine defaults apply. LUNA_JUDGEMENT on The judging ladder over model proposals. off, false, 0, no or disabled switches it off. Off is not a pass: proposals are shown unjudged, and health-adjacent ones still say “not verified”. LUNA_ADMIT_MAX (unset: direct dispatch) Turns on the in-process admission scheduler for vision and photo-plan calls, ordered by level tier. A non-numeric value fails startup. Leave it off while chasing a timeout. LUNA_ADMIT_QUEUE 4 when LUNA_ADMIT_MAX is set The number of callers that may wait behind the admission slots. Never unbounded. LUNA_GATE_MAX_INFLIGHT, LUNA_GATE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS (unset: inert) The shared inference library’s pre-submission backpressure gate. It refuses a request whose remaining deadline can’t cover the wait plus the decode. CORE_ROUTER_BILLING_KEY_FILE, CORE_ROUTER_BILLING_KID (unset: no claim) LUNA’s own signing key (a file path) and its key id. With both set, every model call (chat, plan and meal work, judging and vision) carries a freshly signed platform claim for the product luna, and the model router serves LUNA in its platform lane. The claim is a routing label, not a charge: LUNA is unpriced, its users are never billed for compute, and the claim carries no user data. With either variable unset, the boot log says billing claims off and the router treats LUNA’s calls as spot. A signing failure never fails a call: the call goes out unclaimed and luna_billing_claim_sign_failures_total counts it.
data.limits#Limits: Variable Default Purpose LUNA_RATE_RPS / LUNA_RATE_BURST 5 / 20 Transport rate limit per session. The two defaults apply independently. LUNA_CHAT_TURNS_PER_HOUR 30 Model chat turns per hour. Deterministic plan actions and habit logging are free. 0 disables the cap. LUNA_VISION_CALLS_PER_HOUR 12 Vision calls per hour: meal photos, form review and plan-from-photos. 0 disables the cap. LUNA_VOICE_CALLS_PER_HOUR 120 Transcription plus speech calls per hour. 0 disables the cap. Fixed limits, not configurable: at most 3 images per vision request, 6 MiB per image, 16 MiB of audio per transcription, and a 17 MiB gRPC message cap. Deadlines are 6 minutes for chat, 8 for vision and plans, and 4 for voice.
data.outbound-transport-check#Outbound transp:
Before it opens its listener, the server checks every outbound endpoint: INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL, LUNA_VISION_REMOTE_URL, VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL, LUNA_EMBED_URL, TTSD_URL, CORE_HEALTH_URL and OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT. Cluster-internal plaintext is allowed. Anything else that would carry personal data off the cluster unencrypted stops the process, and the error lists every bad endpoint at once:
luna: N outbound endpoint(s) would carry personal data in cleartext off this cluster: - …
data.serving-and-observability#Serving and ob: Variable Default Purpose PORT 0 (auto-assign) The listen port for gRPC, gRPC-Web, /media/ and the web bundle, all multiplexed on one port. LUNA_WEB_DIR (unset: no static serving) Directory of the Flutter web bundle, served from the same origin as the API. The image sets /app/web. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS * Comma-separated gRPC-Web origins. Same-origin serving needs no CORS in production. APP_VERSION (unset) The version stamped on logs. CORE_HEALTH_URL (unset: no reporting) Where agent health is reported to the Runink TIDE console. It carries a bearer token (CORE_HEALTH_TOKEN).
data.storage#Storage: Variable Default Purpose OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT, OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET, other OBJECTSTORE_* (unset) The platform object store, holding the appfs root and avatar media. The full set is documented by the store library. LUNA_APPFS_DIR a temp directory The local encrypted appfs root. With an object store, it is only the pre-connect fallback for memory and sessions. Without an object store, it is the durable root for everything (local development). LUNA_TIMEZONE UTC IANA timezone that sets the day boundary for streaks and points.
data.voice#Voice: Variable Default Purpose VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL (unset) The in-cluster Voxtral speech-to-text endpoint. When it is unset, Transcribe answers voice transcription not configured (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL unset). TTSD_URL http://ttsd.inference-system.svc.cluster.local:5005/v1/audio/speech The platform’s ttsd speech service. It works with no configuration. Set it to "" to disable server speech, and clients then use on-device TTS. TTSD_CALLER_KEY_FILE (unset: no credential sent) Path to LUNA’s per-caller ttsd service key, mounted by the platform operator (e.g. /etc/runink/ttsd-caller/). It is sent as Authorization: Bearer and re-read on every call, so rotating the key needs no restart. If it is set but the file is missing or empty, the speech call fails instead of going out anonymously, and the app falls back to on-device TTS.

data.cicd#CI/CD: Workflow Trigger What it does ci.yml Every PR and every push to main go build / vet / test in every Go module (with the private sibling libraries checked out), and flutter analyze / test with minimum-test-count ratchets cd.yml Push to main, or workflow_dispatch Builds the image through Runink TIDE’s reusable core-images-build.yml, restarts luna-system/luna, waits for Ready, and warns if the running image digest didn’t change. roll_only restarts without rebuilding. The CD gate is the image build itself, because the Dockerfile compiles Go and builds Flutter web.
data.legacy-data#Legacy data: Records written before per-account scoping sit in a partition called default. They carry no identity and are readable by nobody until an operator runs claim-legacy-data --account . Records from the older record-store layout are copied into appfs by migrate-appfs, which runs after every connect and again 15 minutes later. It is idempotent and never deletes the old objects.
data.network-policy#Network policy:
The deployment manifest, which lives in TIDE’s infrastructure tree, declares a luna-ingress policy and an egress allowlist: DNS, the inference plane, and object storage, plus 443 to external addresses for Google’s JWKS at login. Check the live state with kubectl -n luna-system get netpol.
LUNA’s own controls do not depend on that policy: the startup outbound transport check runs the server only when every endpoint outside the cluster is encrypted, and the backend has no third-party AI code path.
data.persistence-connects-lazily#Persistence:
The object store connects lazily, with retries, plus a background reconnect loop. After a pod restart, the new pod IP can take a minute or two to be admitted by the network policy guarding the object store. During that window dials time out (they are dropped, not refused), and the loop keeps trying until they succeed.
Until the object store connects, memory and sessions use the local encrypted fallback root. Journals are refused honestly during that time: a chat turn still streams, but it is marked not_persisted and the app shows it as “not saved”.
data.pod-posture#Pod posture: Control Status Non-root, no capabilities, read-only root filesystem, no service-account token Enforced by the pod securityContext Allowlist-only access Enforced and fail-closed Secrets from luna-secrets via secretKeyRef, never logged Enforced Personal data leaves the cluster only over encrypted endpoints Enforced at startup by the outbound transport check
data.storage-the-appfs-root#Storage: the appf:
Everything LUNA persists for an account lives in one encrypted, append-only store/appfs root for the app luna. It is sealed under a key derived by HKDF from CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK and kept in the configured bucket on the shared object store:
luna/etc/allowlist.json last allowlist enforced (sessions) luna/home//account hash → address note luna/home//migrated/ migration receipts luna/var/log/. chat_turns, habit_events, avatars, plans, body, training_log luna/var/lib/comet/memory-./ long-term memory (vector index) luna/run/sessions/ sessions is a hash of the account address, not the address itself. The streams are append-only logs. There is no delete path, and an “update” is a superseding append. names the embedding vector space (for example qwen3-embedding-d768). Changing EMBEDDING_FORMAT or LUNA_EMBEDDING_DIM opens a new, empty index. Re-embedding existing memories is a separate platform runbook, and nothing in LUNA runs it. Avatar media is not in appfs. Custom video loops live in the object store’s public media area and are served through signed, expiring URLs. No appfs key can be reached through /media/.
data.the-image#The image:
grpc/Dockerfile builds one image, luna-backend, in three stages:
The Flutter web bundle (cirruslabs/flutter:3.44.0, Dart 3.12.0), built with no source maps. The build fails if a .map file appears. A static Go binary, luna-server (CGO_ENABLED=0). A slim Debian runtime running as numeric UID 1000, with LUNA_WEB_DIR=/app/web and LUNA_AGENT_CONFIG=/app/agents/luna.ini. It exposes 8080, and the entrypoint is /app/luna-server serve. The Flutter image and the pubspec’s Dart floor must move together. A pubspec that needs a newer Dart than the image ships builds locally and fails in-cluster. A CI step compares the two.
One port serves everything: native gRPC, gRPC-Web for the browser, the /media/ proxy for signed avatar-media URLs, and the static web bundle, which shares its origin with the API. There is no /health endpoint. Readiness means the port accepts gRPC (grpcurl … list).

data: Every message below is copied from the code. Server messages reach the app as the gRPC status message, and the app shows them as they are rather than as a raw error. Log lines go to the pod’s stdout.
data.chat-and-the-model#Chat and the model:
Message Cause Luna's own inference server could not be reached. This is not a queue — the model plane is down or not yet configured. Connection refused or no route. Check INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL and the plane. the model plane is busy right now — every slot on the shared inference server is in use. Try again in a moment. The plane answered 429 or 503, or reported being full. the model did not answer in time. It is running, but this request took longer than Luna is willing to wait. The deadline was exceeded (DeadlineExceeded). The chat deadline is 6 minutes. Luna could not complete that generation. The reason is in the server log; it was not a queue and not a timeout. Anything else. Read the pod log. We've talked a lot this hour and the thinking plane is shared — give me about N minutes and ask again. Logging habits and your plans still work instantly. The hourly chat cap (LUNA_CHAT_TURNS_PER_HOUR, default 30) was reached. This refusal is not journaled. Boot log: no INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL set — chat will fail until the inference plane is configured Chat isn’t configured. Boot log: chat tier UNAVAILABLE at after : … — the client stays registered, so requests will still be attempted and will fail slowly rather than fast The plane didn’t come up. … tier ready at (model loaded in ) is the healthy line. In the app, Luna is unreachable — check your connection and try again. means the request never got an answer from the backend.
Request failed with status: 0 in the browser, together with context canceled in the server log, is a transport kill: a mobile NAT, a carrier middlebox or the browser dropped a response that stayed silent too long. Every RPC that waits on the model streams and re-sends a heartbeat beat every 15 seconds for exactly this reason. If you see it, look for an RPC that waits on the model without streaming. Don’t assume the inference plane is down.
data.coaching-preconditions#Coaching precondi: Message Cause design a training plan first — meal targets are derived from the training week, so the two agree. DraftMealPlan was called with no active training plan. I need your body mass in kg first — every target is anchored to it, and guessing would give you numbers computed for someone else. There is no body mass on the request or in the profile. level N costs C points — you have B. Keep the streaks alive. LevelUp was called with too few points. a daily steps goal needs to be between 1,000 and 100,000 SetStepsGoal was out of range. For step-sync messages in the app, see Habits and streaks.
data.sign-in-and-sessions#Sign-in and session: Message Code Cause and fix luna has no allowed accounts configured (LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL unset) FailedPrecondition The allowlist is empty, so every login is rejected. Set LUNA_OWNER_EMAIL. google sign-in not configured: google sign-in not configured (LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset) FailedPrecondition Set LUNA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. this account is not on this luna instance's allowlist PermissionDenied A valid Google account that isn’t on the list. google email not verified / invalid google token Unauthenticated A token problem on the user’s side. cannot reach Google to verify this sign-in — this is a server-side connectivity problem, not a problem with your account: … Unavailable The backend can’t reach Google’s keys. Check egress on 443. authorization token is not provided Unauthenticated The request had no Bearer token. invalid token: … Unauthenticated An unknown, expired or revoked session. The app signs out and returns to the login screen. session email is not on this luna instance's allowlist PermissionDenied The account was removed from the list. Its sessions are revoked. luna's session store is unavailable Unavailable The appfs root couldn’t be mounted, usually because CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK is missing. The server can’t check anything, so the caller’s token is not the problem.
data.startup-refusals#Startup refusals: Message Cause luna: N outbound endpoint(s) would carry personal data in cleartext off this cluster: followed by a list An outbound URL points off-cluster over plaintext. Every bad endpoint is listed, so you can fix the manifest in one pass. admission config: … LUNA_ADMIT_MAX or LUNA_ADMIT_QUEUE isn’t a valid number.
data.storage-and-memory#Storage and memory: Log event or message Cause object_store_not_configured: “OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT unset and no LUNA_APPFS_DIR; journals, plans and avatars cannot persist” No storage at all. Nothing persists. appfs_local_root_online No object store, but LUNA_APPFS_DIR names a real directory, which then holds everything (local development). object_store_recovered A background retry succeeded. This is normal shortly after a pod restart. object_store_still_down: “…a Secret this pod cannot resolve (CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK, OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY) fails here exactly like an unreachable objectd, and no retry clears it” This is no longer transient. Read the logged error first. A missing Secret looks exactly like a network fault. “the at-rest encryption key (CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK) is not configured, and the object store refuses to open a store whose contents it cannot seal” The KEK is missing. no account on this request — Luna's storage is per-account and will not read or write without one The data layer refused an unscoped request. This fails closed by design. A reply marked “not saved” (not_persisted) The journal write failed or timed out (bounded at 5 s). The reply was delivered, but it won’t be remembered. memory: semantic recall INACTIVE: … No embedding tier (LUNA_EMBED_URL unset or unreachable). Memory falls back to keyword search only. refusing to start: EMBEDDING_FORMAT: … An unknown embedding format. The server won’t open a memory index in a vector space nobody configured.
data.vision#Vision: Message Cause my eyes aren't wired to a vision model yet — the platform needs its vision tier online for this LUNA_VISION_REMOTE_URL is unset (FailedPrecondition). The text model can’t see images, so there is deliberately no fallback. vision is rate-limited on the shared plane — try again in ~N min The hourly vision cap (default 12) was reached. N photos is more than I can look at in one go — send up to 3 at a time More than 3 images in one request. The app batches for you. Lowering the server cap without shipping a new app build makes every batch fail.
data.voice#Voice: Message Cause voice transcription not configured (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL unset) STT isn’t configured. The app falls back to the device recogniser. text-to-speech not configured TTSD_URL is set to "". The app falls back to on-device TTS. Server log: tts: reading the ttsd caller key (TTSD_CALLER_KEY_FILE=…) or tts: the ttsd caller key file (…) is empty The caller-key Secret is not mounted, or is empty. Nothing is sent to ttsd, and the app falls back to on-device TTS. Check the ttsd-caller-key-luna Secret and its mount. voice transcription is rate-limited on the shared plane — try again in ~N min / voice is rate-limited on the shared plane — try again in ~N min The hourly voice cap (default 120) was reached. Boot log: voice output DEGRADED: ttsd unreachable at after ( attempts): … ttsd never answered its health probe during the retry window. The healthy line is voice output: ttsd ready at . The probe is advisory and gates nothing. Boot log: voice output disabled (TTSD_URL empty) — clients use on-device TTS Server speech was turned off on purpose. An unreachable ttsd is invisible to users, because the app quietly falls back to the device voice. That is why the boot probe logs its result.
